title: Workforce Management Information - Department for Work and Pensions
description:
"Monthly management information on staff numbers and paybill costs in Civil Service departments, their agencies and their executive NDPBs.
For workforce numbers, both payroll and non-payroll (contingent labour, including consultants) information is provided, split between full-time equivalents (FTE) and headcount, with payroll staff numbers mapped to standard Civil Service grades.
For costs, payroll paybill information is broken down into its component parts i.e. salaries, allowances, employers pensions contributions etc. For non-payroll costs, these are split between costs for consultancy and those of other non-payroll workers.
Staffing numbers are as at the last day of the month for the reference month. Cost information is that for the reference month. For baseline 2010/11 returns, staffing numbers are as at 31 March 2011, and paybill costs are for the financial year 2010/11."

title: Rezago habitacional
description: El rezago habitacional es una medición que caracteriza y cuantifica a las viviendas en situación de precariedad tanto en su construcción como en su condición de habitabilidad. Una vivienda se encuentra en condición de rezago habitacional cuando se cumple con al menos una de las siguientes características: alguno de sus elementos básicos (paredes, techo o pisos) esté construido con materiales no adecuados; la vivienda no cuenta con excusado; o sus habitantes se encuentran en hacinamiento (residen 2.5 o más personas por cuarto).

title: Saldo Histórico de los Requerimientos Financieros del Sector Público (SHRFSP - Deuda Amplia) - De 2014 a la fecha
description: Saldo histórico de los requerimientos financieros del sector público (SHRFSP), que representa el acervo neto de las obligaciones contraídas para alcanzar los objetivos de las políticas públicas, tanto de las entidades adscritas al sector público como de las entidades privadas que actúan por cuenta del Gobierno Federal. Es decir, pasivos menos activos financieros disponibles, por concesión de préstamos y por fondos para la amortización de la deuda, como reflejo de la trayectoria anual observada a lo largo del tiempo de los RFSP. El SHRFSP ahora agrupa a la deuda neta del sector público presupuestario y las obligaciones netas del IPAB, del FONADIN, los asociados a PIDIREGAS y a los Programas de Apoyo a Deudores, así como la pérdida esperada de la banca de desarrollo y fondos de fomento.

title: Texas State Expenditures By County 2024
description:
Texas State Expenditures by County shows where state dollars are spent. It lists state expenditures by agency and type of expenditure in each county. This report was created using information from the state's Uniform Statewide Accounting System. It reflects actual net expenditures of funds from accounts held in the State Treasury during the state's fiscal year, Sept. 1 through Aug. 31.

The data is available through the Texas Open Data Portal, can be filtered as needed and is downloadable for further analysis. PDF file reports predating 2017 can be provided upon request by emailing transparency@cpa.texas.gov.

title: Tree Removal Permits
description:
This dataset shows issued tree removal permits in Cambridge. 

For any Significant Tree removal, a permit is required from the City Arborist and subject to rules and regulations under City of Cambridge’s Tree Protection Ordinance, Title 8, Chapter 8.66, of the City’s Municipal Code.

A Significant Tree is defined as any tree that has a diameter equal to or greater than six inches (6”) measured at breast height (4.5 feet above the ground). A Mitigation Payment will be required for all Significant Trees removed where an insufficient quantity of Replacement Trees is provided.

For more information, please visit https://www.cambridgema.gov/iwantto/applyforatreeremovalpermit

title: A monthly 1° global ocean mixed layer depth dataset for 1982–2023 developed with SJTU-ViT
description: This dataset provides monthly global ocean mixed layer depth (MLD) estimates at 1° spatial resolution from January 1982 to December 2023, developed using SJTU-ViT, a Vision Transformer-based reconstruction model. It contains 504 monthly fields on a regular latitude–longitude grid, with valid coverage defined by a fixed RECCAP2 open-ocean mask. The target MLD is defined by a potential density increase of 0.03 kg m⁻³ relative to 10 m. MLD estimates are expressed in metres, positive downward from the sea surface, with a lower bound of 10 m. Data are provided in NetCDF-4 format, accompanied by a README describing the variables, coordinates, MLD definition, masking, and data access. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23463931

title: A transient simulation of global vegetation dynamics over the past 20,000 years
description: This repository accompanies “A transient simulation of global vegetation dynamics over the past 20,000 years”. It provides simulations of potential natural vegetation and associated land-surface variables generated with ORCHIDEE-MICT, together with factorial experiments, model source code, configuration information and forcing-processing scripts. The main transient simulation spans 20,000 years before present (BP) to 1999 CE. BP is referenced to 1950 CE, so the annual age coordinate runs from 20,000 to −49 BP. The simulations use prescribed climate and atmospheric CO₂. Climate forcing is derived from TraCE-21K-II, with bias correction and within-month temporal disaggregation based on CRU-JRA v2.2 for 1901–1920, as described in the accompanying manuscript. The files use the TraCE-21K-II T31 grid (approximately 3.75° resolution), with 96 longitude coordinates and 48 Gaussian latitude coordinates.  Transient simulation outputs Data_transient_annual.zip contains eight NetCDF files, which are annual-mean outputs from the transient simulation: •    Veg_annual.nc : fractional cover for each archived PFT category.  •     LAI_annual.nc : leaf area index aggregated across PFTs. •     GPP_annual.nc and NPP_annual.nc : gross and net primary productivity aggregated across PFTs. •     Biomass_annual.nc : plant biomass carbon stock aggregated across PFTs. •     Evap_annual.nc : evapotranspiration rate. •     Snowdz_annual.nc : annual mean snow depth. •     Megabiome_annual.nc : megabiome classifications derived from the simulated vegetation. Megabiome codes are 1: tropical forest; 2: warm-temperate forest; 3: savanna and dry woodland; 4: grassland and dry shrubland; 5: warm desert; 6: temperate forest; 7: boreal forest; and 8: tundra and polar desert. These files use the dimensions year , lat and lon ; Veg_annual.nc additionally has a pft dimension. The archived PFT categories comprise bare ground, eight tree PFTs and two natural grass PFTs. PFTname identifies the categories in their stored order. Common mask variables ( landfrac and icefrac ) are included in each file. SoilT_monthly_<start>_to_<end>.nc and SoilM_monthly_<start>_to_<end>.nc contain monthly soil temperature and soil water content, respectively. They use the dimensions year , mon , depth , lat and lon , with six archived soil-temperature levels and four soil-moisture levels. These files are divided into time intervals to limit file size. The file naming follows a left-closed, right-open interval ([startyr, endyr)), i.e., startyr ≤ year < endyr . The decreasing BP coordinate follows the simulation forward in chronological time. Factorial experiment outputs Data_factorial.zip contains CTRL.nc , fixCO2.nc , fixP.nc , fixT.nc , fixTcold.nc and fixTwarm.nc . Each file contains 36 independent time-slice simulations. CTRL is the all-forcing snapshot control. The other experiments hold atmospheric CO₂, precipitation, temperature, coldest-quarter temperature or warmest-quarter temperature, respectively, at the LGM conditions specified in the experimental design. For each time slice, a randomly selected 20-year forcing sequence is repeated to drive 200 model years to reach equilibrium for vegetation. Archived variables summarize the final 20 model years. The time coordinate identifies the 36 TraCE-21K-II forcing segments; it does not represent 36 consecutive years. The segment chronology and experimental settings are described in the accompanying manuscript. Factorial comparisons document sensitivity to the prescribed forcing changes and should be interpreted in the context of this snapshot protocol. Code and configuration ORCHIDEE.zip contains the model source code. The ORCHIDEE version used in this study is ORCHIDEE-MICT (r5308). It is open source and distributed under the CeCILL (CEA CNRS INRIA Logiciel Libre

title: AI-DRIVEN ONLINE ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF LEARNER MODELLING, ADAPTATION MECHANISMS AND EVIDENCE OF EFFECTIVENESS
description: The rapid expansion of online and blended learning in higher education has exposed a persistent limitation of conventional online courses: content is delivered to all students in the same sequence and at the same pace, regardless of differences in prior knowledge, learning progress and needs. Online adaptive learning systems, increasingly powered by artificial intelligence (AI), aim to overcome this limitation by continuously diagnosing the learner and personalising content, sequence, difficulty and feedback. Aim. This article reviews the theoretical foundations, learner-modelling techniques, adaptation mechanisms and empirical evidence on the effectiveness of AI-driven online adaptive learning systems, and derives implications for higher education systems undergoing digital transformation, with particular reference to Uzbekistan. Methods. An integrative literature review was conducted following the framework of Whittemore and Knafl. Seminal works and peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC and Google Scholar, together with international policy documents, were analysed using reflexive thematic synthesis. Results. Six themes were identified: (1) pedagogical and psychological foundations; (2) learner modelling, from Bayesian knowledge tracing to deep learning; (3) adaptation targets and mechanisms; (4) evidence of effectiveness from meta-analyses; (5) the emerging role of generative AI; and (6) ethical, pedagogical and infrastructural challenges. Meta-analytic evidence shows moderate to large positive effects of intelligent and adaptive tutoring on learning outcomes, while gaps remain regarding teacher involvement, transparency and applicability to low-resource language contexts. Conclusion. Effective adaptive learning requires the integration of validated learner models, pedagogically grounded adaptation rules, interoperable learning platforms and a teacher-in-the-loop approach. A set of requirements for national adaptive learning systems is proposed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23385110

title: ALISHER NAVOI'S "MUHOKAMAT UL-LUG'ATAYN" AS AN INVALUABLE MASTERPIECE OF LINGUISTICS
description: This article examines the linguistic, historical, and cultural significance of Alisher Navoi’s Muhokamat ul-Lug‘atayn (The Comparison of Two Languages) as an outstanding monument of linguistic thought. Particular attention is paid to Navoi’s comparative analysis of Turkic and Persian, his arguments concerning the expressive capabilities of the Turkic language, and his contribution to the development of linguistic consciousness and literary identity. The study employs historical-comparative, descriptive, and textual-analytical approaches to explore the principal linguistic ideas presented in the treatise. The analysis demonstrates that Navoi’s work addresses issues of lexical richness, semantic differentiation, linguistic expression, and the relationship between language and literary creativity. The article also considers the relevance of Navoi’s linguistic heritage to contemporary discussions of multilingualism, language preservation, and cultural identity. It concludes that Muhokamat ul-Lug‘atayn remains an important source for understanding the history of Turkic linguistic thought and the intellectual traditions of Central Asia. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23595376
tags: ["Alisher Navoi, Muhokamat ul-Lug'atayn, comparative linguistics, Turkic language, Persian language, historical linguistics, lexical semantics, linguistic heritage, literary language, cultural identity."]

title: AN ANALYSIS OF HOUSING PRICES IN TASHKENT: THE EFFECTS OF PROPERTY SIZE AND LOCATION!
description: This study examines the relationship between property size, location, and housing prices in Tashkent. Using a dataset of 100 residential property listings, the study analyzes average and median prices, price per square meter, and differences across districts. The analysis finds a strong positive relationship between property size and total price, with a correlation coefficient of 0.705. District-level analysis also shows differences in average price per square meter, suggesting that location plays an important role in housing prices. Mirzo-Ulugbek had the highest average price per square meter among the districts analyzed, while Mirabad had the highest average total property price. These findings suggest that both property size and location are important factors associated with housing prices in Tashkent. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23561763

title: AZ-Hydro — Historical and Projected Arizona Annual Water Use: Software, Input Data, Models, Raster and Well Package Predictions, and Validation at 2 km Resolution (1896–2099)
description: AZ-Hydro: Historical and Projected Arizona Annual Water Use, 1896–2099 (v1.2) A 2 km-resolution gridded dataset of Arizona groundwater and surface-water withdrawals, irrigation consumptive use, and pumping-induced stream capture, spanning 204 years (1896–2099), with per-pixel uncertainty from a six-component framework and a well-level package for ~170,000 registered consumptive wells. Companion data archive for Majumdar et al. (in prep., Nature Scientific Data ; preprint https://doi.org/10.31223/X56N63 ) and Majumdar et al. (in prep., AGU Earth’s Future ). Version 1.2 (code release v1.2.0). See What’s new in v1.2 below. What’s in this deposit File Size Contents Audience az-hydro-headline.7z ~8.7 GB Self-contained subset of every key output: six-band augmented per-pixel, per-year withdrawal, consumptive-use, and stream capture rasters (prediction, σ, CV, SNR, lower and upper 95 % CI); the GeoParquet well package; per-basin and per-sub-basin time series; the CAP shortage-scenario sweep; era-mean and trend figures; validation and intercomparison outputs. Most users want this. Reviewers and downstream users of the published product az-hydro-data.7z ~80 GB Full reproducibility archive (~220 GB uncompressed): everything in the headline archive plus the raw inputs, cross-validation outputs, intermediate input stacks, and per-component uncertainty rasters (σ_MACA, σ_model, σ_irr, σ_LULC, σ_GW, σ_USBR, σ_CU). Anyone re-running the pipeline from scratch az-hydro-1.2.0.zip ~64 MB Tagged source-code release (Python pipeline, GEE export and upload scripts, documentation), identical to the GitHub repository at tag v1.2.0. Anyone running the pipeline Inside each .7z , Data/HEADLINE_README.md (headline archive) or Data/README.md (full archive) gives the per-directory inventory and the external-source citations. How to unpack the .7z files The archives use LZMA2 with solid-block compression, which macOS Archive Utility cannot open. Use one of: macOS : Keka or The Unarchiver Windows : 7-Zip , WinRAR , or Bandizip Linux : p7zip (for example apt install p7zip-full , then 7z x az-hydro-data.7z ) What’s new in v1.2 Post-2026 Colorado River shortage. The central projection now uses the 2027–2028 Operating Guidelines (U.S. Department of the Interior, August 2026), which reduce Arizona’s Colorado River apportionment by 760 kAF yr⁻¹ (CAP delivery factor 0.49, groundwater boost 7.5). The guidelines cover 2027–2028; 2029–2099 hold that latest official condition as a stand-in for continued shortage, not as a forecast. v1.0–v1.1 held the Tier 1 cut (512 kAF yr⁻¹) through 2099. Projected 2027–2099 groundwater withdrawal is 5.5 % higher and surface-water withdrawal 5.5 % lower than in v1.1; total withdrawal and all 1896–2026 predictions are unchanged. CAP scenario sweep. A ninth scenario applies the 2027–2028 Operating Guidelines: 652 kAF yr⁻¹ of CAP delivery, the 900 kAF yr⁻¹ post-Tier baseline less the 248 kAF yr⁻¹ by which the guidelines’ 760 kAF yr⁻¹ Arizona reduction exceeds the Tier 1 cut that baseline is taken to include. It adds 1.30 MAF of groundwater pumping over 2027–2060 and 3.15 MAF over 2027–2099. The other scenarios are unchanged. Uncertainty ensemble. The ensemble members now apply the same dynamic CAP caps and floors as the central partition (a missing import had disabled them). σ for the groundwater and surface-water categories changes in every year; σ for total withdrawal does not. The scenario sweep keeps its full-delivery counterfactual. ADWR partner CSVs ( Outputs/.../ADWR/ ). In v1.1, 14 of the 16 CSVs listed every basin-year twice, because the export also picked up the all-basin aggregate files. Each row now appears once, and Total_Predicted is built from the same per-basin series as the other categories, so Total_GW + Total_SW = Total_

title: BAM Landbird Density & Habitat Models
description: This dataset contains the publicly released outputs from the Boreal Avian Modelling Project’s Version 5.0 landbird density and habitat models. It provides 1-km GeoTIFF prediction mosaics for Canada, Alaska, and the contiguous United States (Lower 48), together with model validation and abundance summaries, summarized marginal effects, predictor-importance estimates, modelling-region geometry, and supporting metadata. The raster products report mean predicted male density, uncertainty across model bootstraps, and effective detection distance. Only models approved for public release are included; raw observations, model-training data, fitted model objects, and individual-region prediction rasters are excluded. These products supersede and expand upon the earlier Version 4.0 release . Code for the production of these products is available at https://github.com/borealbirds/LandbirdModelsV5. title: Beyond Digitalization: Mapping the Digital Capability–ESG Nexus in Sustainable Supply Chains
description: Digital transformation has expanded the technological capabilities of supply chains, yet its integration with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) priorities remains conceptually fragmented. This study examines the research landscape connecting digital capability, ESG orientation, and sustainable supply chain management through bibliometric analysis and structured literature synthesis. A Scopus search conducted on October 15, 2026, yielded 72 publications from 2021–2026, analyzed using VOSviewer and R-based Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny. The findings reveal that 81.94\% of publications appeared during 2025–2026, spanning 60 scientific sources, with international co-authorship accounting for 34.72\%. Keyword co-occurrence and thematic analyses identify digital transformation, artificial intelligence, circular economy, supply chain management, and sustainability as prominent research themes. However, digital capability and green innovation occupy relatively peripheral thematic positions, while explicit ESG terminology remains sparsely represented. These findings highlight a conceptual disconnect between technology-driven sustainability research and integrated ESG-oriented supply chain governance. This study contributes to the literature by mapping the evolving knowledge structure and identifying future research priorities involving organizational digital capabilities, interorganizational transparency, green innovation, and multidimensional sustainability performance. The findings provide a foundation for advancing intelligent, responsible, and sustainability-oriented supply chain research. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23407800

title: Borrowed Youth and the Geography of Production Investment: Article and Replication Materials
description: Borrowed Youth and the Geography of Production Investment develops a temporal theory of demographic location advantage. Opening workforces, local cohorts and international replacement routes provide distinct dated services. Capital duration can reverse country rankings; home-linked recruitment and shared foreign affiliates change the switching threshold, while border institutions distinguish recruitment cost from permission to obtain workers. Public article and replication, version 3.20.0, 23 October 2026. Start with README.txt. The current manuscript, online appendix and complete LaTeX are directly downloadable. The three current verified ZIP blocks, manifest and restoration helper combine with the nine frozen complementary base archives to reconstruct the complete 1,836-file replication tree and verify 1,835 checksum entries. Earlier article overlays are historical. Regression tables report p-values to three decimal places, using p<0.001 for smaller values and no significance stars. Missing probabilities are supplied from held full-precision estimates and their stated cluster, permutation or bootstrap inference. The publication_reporting module reconstructs the corrected LaTeX, all six editable RTF table files and economic magnitudes. The economic discussion translates coefficients into conditional percentage and currency comparisons with uncertainty; the regressions and observations are unchanged. The demographic-renewal flagship and all five earlier figures are retained. European manufacturing comparisons and 299 foreign-country allocations retain common-support uncertainty and the joint-test outcomes. The held panels establish neither joint support nor a familywise contradiction; they are not an identified prospective host-choice experiment. The reference-fee envelope makes its attainable-flow, tenure, cost and contribution-margin assumptions explicit. Original work is CC BY 4.0; third-party sources retain their own licences and attribution. The Lyons dissertation is linked to its original TARA repository and is not republished. Factual coding and numerical reconstruction are included; source-page rechecking additionally requires the original PDF. Licensed WRDS observations are excluded; subscriber queries and aggregate outputs are supplied. The article has 9,894 counted words, a 194-word abstract, 23 full substantive text pages before references, six figures and three tables. The manuscript has 41 pages and online appendix 122. The page-41 AI declaration reads: ChatGPT and Codex (OpenAI) were used in October 2026 for coding help, literature search, and red teaming and review. Reviewer files retain anonymous formatting; public repository metadata supplies author attribution. This public research deposit does not constitute journal submission or acceptance. title: CAMELS-PL: hydro-meteorological time series and landscape attributes for 869 catchments in Poland
description: Description: CAMELS-PL provides a comprehensive collection of hydro-meteorological time series and catchment attributes for 869 streamflow gauges across Poland. The hydrological time series (discharge and water level) span from 1 January 1951 to 31 October 2025; the meteorological time series derived from E-OBS v33.0e span from 1 January 1951 to 31 October 2025; the supplementary meteorological time series derived from G2DC-PL+ span from 1 January 1951 to 31 December 2019; and the benchmark model simulations (LSTM and HBV) cover the full modelled period from 1 January 1951 to 31 October 2025. All time series are in daily resolution. The static catchment attributes include information about topography (derived from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and a national 10 m DEM), climate, hydrology, soils (derived from SoilGrids250m and the Polish SWAT soil database, which also provides soil hydraulic properties), and land cover derived from both the European CORINE Land Cover 2018 dataset and the national BDOT10k topographic database. Catchment boundaries and gauging station locations are provided as shapefiles and GeoPackage files and were obtained from IMGW-PIB. Additionally, the dataset includes discharge simulations from a regionally trained Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, which uses static soil attributes from the Polish SWAT soil database, and a locally calibrated conceptual HBV model, providing benchmark data for future hydrological modelling studies in Poland. Potential evapotranspiration is provided using both the Hargreaves and the Penman equations; the HBV model was calibrated with Hargreaves. Information about the code and methods for generating CAMELS-PL can be found here: https://github.com/bigapple233-cmyk/Hy2DL/tree/CAMELS-PL Disclaimer: Discharge, water level time series, and catchment boundary data included in CAMELS-PL were obtained from the Institute of Meteorology and Water Management — National Research Institute (IMGW-PIB). For terms of use, please refer to:  https://danepubliczne.imgw.pl Catchment-aggregated meteorological time series derived from E-OBS are excluded from CC BY 4.0 and are subject to the ECA&D/E-OBS Data Policy. Changelog v2.0.0 Extended release of CAMELS-PL, expanding the dataset from 354 to 869 catchments across Poland. Includes daily hydrological time series for 869 catchments across Poland (1 January 1951 – 31 October 2025). Includes daily meteorological time series derived from E-OBS v33.0e for 869 catchments across Poland (1 January 1951 – 31 October 2025). Includes catchment attributes covering topography (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and national 10 m DEM), climate, hydrology, soils (SoilGrids250m and Polish SWAT soil database), CORINE land cover, and BDOT10k national land cover. Includes simulated discharge time series and benchmark results from a regional LSTM model (5 ensemble members) and a locally calibrated HBV model (5 calibration seeds using the DREAM algorithm). Includes potential evapotranspiration estimated using the Hargreaves and Penman equations. Includes HBV model parameter sets and LSTM model training epoch files for all ensemble members. Includes supplementary meteorological time series from the G2DC-PL+ gridded dataset for 869 catchments across Poland (1 January 1951 – 31 December 2019). DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23102156

title: CARINA.WP2.T2.5.2.Biostimulator_Germination_Tests_Serbia
description: This dataset contains information on the efficacy of KIMITEC-supplied biostimulant candidates, including wood vinegar and the formulations CARI-03 and CAMEL-03, on seed germination dynamics and antioxidant status under abiotic stress conditions. Wood vinegar was tested on tomato seeds under salinity and heat stress, while CARI-03 and CAMEL-03 were evaluated on oilseed rape, pepper, tomato, and maize under salinity stress. The experiments were conducted under controlled laboratory conditions at Laboratory for Seed Testing and Laboratory for Testing Plant Materials and Products of the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops (IFVCNS), Novi Sad, Serbia, within the Horizon Europe project CARINA. The dataset includes quantitative data on seed germination and seedling growth parameters, including germination energy (first count), final germination percentage, atypical seedlings, non-germinated seeds, mean germination time, germination rate, shoot length, and root length. Biochemical parameters include chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids, total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, and proline content. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23314798

title: CONGO-CRIMEAN HAEMORRHAGIC FEVER (CCHF): THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SITUATION IN 2026, RANGE EXPANSION AND PREVENTION STRATEGIES
description: Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever is one of the most widespread tick-borne viral haemorrhagic infections in humans, having been reported in more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Europe [5;7;8;11]. The primary vector and reservoir of the virus are ticks of the genus Hyalomma , and the geographical distribution of the disease generally follows their range [3;15;17]. Annually,  10,000–15,000 cases are reported worldwide, with around 3 billion people living in risk areas [7;11;12;17]. However, the true burden of the disease is underestimated due to subclinical infections, inconsistent surveillance and limited laboratory diagnosis [2;7;8;12;18].  This article is based on a synthesis of 20 publications from 2006 to 2026, including reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, national surveillance data and regional outbreak studies [2;10;14;15]. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23393260

description: Event data (one row per detector hit, plus one row per bunch without a hit) of the four acquisitions of the 6s 2S1/2 -> 8p 2P1/2 and 6s 2S1/2 -> 8p 2P3/2 transitions of 133Cs recorded during the commissioning of the CREMA collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup at MIT, and the analysis code (Jupyter notebooks and the Python package crema) that produces the hyperfine constants of Table 2 and Fig. 6 of the accompanying article, including the correction of a 60 Hz modulation of the beam energy with a hidden Markov model; and the oscilloscope measurement of the 60 Hz oscillation of the high-voltage platform (harmonic fits of every trace) with the notebook that gives its amplitude at 0 and 10 kV. title: California Wildfire Perimeters with Environmental and WUI Attributes
description: This dataset contains processed fire perimeter records from four wildfire datasets: the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CalFire; 1990–2025), Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity (MTBS; 1990–2024), the Global Fire Atlas (Atlas; 2001–2025), and the FIREDpy-based country-level dataset (FIRED; 2000–2024). Atlas and FIRED are derived from MODIS imagery. CalFire records are limited to fire events larger than 1 km². All four shapefiles include fire identifiers, ignition date, year and decade, burned area (size_km2), Northern/Southern California flags, and WUI classification attributes from intersecting fire perimeters with WUI boundaries (FireType: WUI vs Wildland; reachWUI; reachUrban). CalFire further includes containment date, ignition cause, climate and terrain variables (temperature, vapor pressure deficit, precipitation, wind, elevation, slope, NDVI, and land cover), ignition-based WUI classes derived by matching Global Fire Atlas ignition points to CalFire perimeters (IgnWUI; IgnType: WUIIgnite, WUISpread, or Wildland), the within-perimeter WUI burned-area fraction (WUIfrac), 4-day mean Canadian Fire Weather Index moisture codes (FFMC_4d, DMC_4d, DC_4d), Santa Ana wind occurrence flags for Southern California fires (SAW), and within-perimeter land-cover fractions from MCD12Q1 FAO-LCCS1 2020 (fracFor, fracGrass, fracShrub, fracSG). A full field list is provided in CalFire_added_fields.txt. The four perimeter datasets are provided as compressed Shapefiles. These data are intended to support research on fire size distribution, fire behavior, land-fire interactions, and WUI risk assessment. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23223977

title: Chlorophyll-a biomass (2008-2022) interpolated to a 0.0833 degree rectangular grid
description: This dataset contains two-dimensional (2D; longitude–latitude) spatially interpolated biogeochemical data derived from the CMEMS Global Ocean Biogeochemistry Hindcast . The original data, provided on a regular 0.25° × 0.25° spatial grid, were regridded to a finer resolution of 0.08333° × 0.08333° using bilinear interpolation. This spatial harmonization was performed to match the grid resolution and geographical alignment of the Continuous Plankton Recorder (CPR) Survey zooplankton dataset provided for the Akvaplan-niva (APN) use case within the DIVE project. The resulting dataset enables direct spatial integration of biogeochemical variables with zooplankton observations, facilitating environmental data extraction, comparative analyses, and the investigation of relationships between oceanographic conditions and zooplankton distributions. Although the interpolation increases the spatial sampling density, it does not increase the intrinsic spatial resolution of the original CMEMS hindcast data. The spatial domain extends in 3D from 20W-29E, 65N-79E down to ca. 16 m (= 10 z-levels). Chlorophyll-a biomass is given in mg/m^3 Further details can be found in the embedded metadata in the netcdf file. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23392001

Equation, table and figure numbers in the README files refer to the paper and the SI. CocoSat24 is a benchmark set of 24 experimental core-level shake-up spectra (8 C 1s, 7 N 1s, 9 O 1s) of 23 conjugated organic molecules with up to 40 atoms. title: Code and Supporting Materials for "Modelo Predictivo de Riesgo Crediticio por Tramos de Mora bajo el Enfoque de la Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP del Perú"
description: This repository contains the source code, Google Colab notebooks, methodological documentation, metadata, and aggregated experimental results used in the master's thesis “Modelo Predictivo de Riesgo Crediticio por Tramos de Mora bajo el Enfoque de la Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP del Perú”. The study evaluates multiclass credit-risk classification models based on delinquency ranges established by the Peruvian Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and Private Pension Funds (SBS), comparing scenarios without external factors and with external factors related to COVID-19, climate conditions, and social unrest. The computational experiments were developed and executed in Google Colab using Python. The repository includes the materials required to reproduce the analytical workflow, including data-preparation procedures, model-training notebooks, evaluation metrics, sensitivity analyses, and statistical significance tests. The original credit-level dataset provided by the financial institution is not publicly included due to confidentiality and data-protection restrictions. Public external-factor sources, metadata, code, and aggregated outputs are provided to support transparency and reproducibility. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23231907

description: # Code and data for "A Benford's Law-Inspired Deep Learning Model for Streamflow Prediction"   Jun Guo, Xinyu Chang, Yi Liu\*, Hui Qin, Shuang Zhu, Yunhui Bai, Shuhui Yang, Xiaojiong Xu   School of Civil and Hydraulic Engineering, and Hubei Key Laboratory of Digital River Basin Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, China. \*Corresponding author: Yi Liu (prof_liuyi@hust.edu.cn)   This package holds what is needed to reproduce every number, table and figure in the paper (submitted to *Journal of Hydrology*) and its supplementary material:   - the input data of the 463 CAMELS basins; - the training, evaluation, analysis and plotting code; - the trained models, the daily simulations of all models and the per-basin metrics.   The study trains one regional LSTM on 463 CAMELS basins. title: Computational Data: Delocalized MLCT States in a Trinuclear Iron Complex
description: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to assess the structural and electronic properties of [Fe NHC ] and [Fe NHC -(Fe CN ) 2 ] with relaxed singlet and triplet ground states (S 0 and T 1 ). A modified hybrid functional with 10% exact exchange and based on the standard B3LYP functional was used in combination with the def2-SVP all electron basis set. A microsolvation environment (water) and dispersive correction was applied to account for implicit effects using a polarizable continuum model and a limited number of explicit water molecules in the first solvent shell ( [Fe NHC ] : two water molecules; [Fe NHC -(Fe CN ) 2 ] : 20 water molecules). Time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) simulations were carried out to evaluate the electronic transitions underlying the electronic absorption as well as involving the time-resolved absorption spectra. The repository contains all fully relaxed equilibrium structures in XYZ-format (singlet ground state, S 0 , as well as lowest energy triplet state, T 1 ) as obtained for [Fe NHC ] and [Fe NHC -(Fe CN ) 2 ] . High resolution PNGs (and CUBE-files) are provided for key electronic singlet-singlet, singlet-triplet and triplet-triplet transitions contributing to the UVvis spectra as well as the simulated TA signature. Further, as well as spin densities and displacement vectors of key vibrational normal modes are given.   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23392133

title: DARK ARs and AR-children tags (ERA5, 1979–2025; q098)
description: This dataset provides annual atmospheric-river (AR) masks and parent–child tracking fields derived from the ERA5 reanalysis using the DARK + Children workflow. It combines the DARK AR-detection algorithm, formerly Buffet v1.0, with a temporal-tracking extension designed to identify the moisture remnants of ARs after Antarctic landfall. The product is evaluated on the full global ERA5 grid, although the tracking extension is designed for Antarctic applications. The dataset contains 6-hourly fields for every year from 1979 to 2025 on the native ERA5 0.25° × 0.25° grid. Scientific reference Please cite the associated methodological paper when using this dataset: Buffet, V., Favier, V., Pohl, B., and Wille, J. D.: Curved atmospheric rivers and their moisture remnants: a new detection tool for Antarctica , Weather and Climate Dynamics, 7, 1189–1210, 2026. https://doi.org/10.5194/wcd-7-1189-2026 Input data The workflow uses ERA5 vertically integrated water-vapour flux components: viwve : vertically integrated eastward water-vapour flux; viwvn : vertically integrated northward water-vapour flux. Integrated Vapor Transport (IVT) is calculated from these two components. The tracking extension also uses a land–sea mask ( lsm ). Grid cells with lsm > 0 are treated as land or ice and are used to define the Antarctic landfall region. DARK AR detection For each leap day-of-year, a 15-day rolling climatology of IVT is calculated over the ERA5 reference period 1979–2025. The local 98th-percentile IVT value defines a seasonally varying threshold at each grid cell. For non-leap years, dates on and after 29 February are mapped to leap-year day-of-year values by shifting the day-of-year by one. A grid cell is initially retained when its IVT exceeds the corresponding local daily threshold. Candidate AR regions are then filtered as follows: connected components are identified using 8-connectivity; longitude is periodic, preserving continuity across the dateline; components smaller than 200,000 km² are removed; component area is calculated on WGS-84 using the local geocentric radius and latitude–longitude spacing; each remaining component is skeletonized and represented as a graph; the endpoint-to-endpoint path best aligned with the component principal axis is selected, extended to the component edges, and smoothed with a B-spline; geodesic segment lengths are calculated on WGS-84; components shorter than 2,000 km are removed. The resulting binary field identifies detected AR structures. Parent–child tracking extension The DARK + Children extension adds time-continuous tracking to the detected AR structures. At each 6-hourly timestep, the exceedance mask is labelled into 8-connected components with periodic longitude boundaries. Labels are matched between consecutive timesteps by maximum pixel overlap, producing continuous AR tracks. Each persistent structure is assigned a track identifier. A component classified as an AR is initially designated as a parent AR. For each track, if a structure overlaps a parent AR and subsequently intersects the Antarctic land mask, later portions of that track are classified as children. Children therefore represent AR fragments or moisture-remnant structures that retain strong IVT after the parent AR reaches Antarctica. An optional geographic filter can retain only parent systems originating outside Antarctica. This can be based on their latitude, for example north of 65° S, and/or on an ocean-origin criterion using the land–sea mask. Files and format One NetCDF file is provided per year: ERA5.ar_children_tag.DARK_children.q098.6hourly.YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD.nc The q098 suffix identifies the 98th-percentile IVT threshold, which is the DARK reference configuration. Each file contains two byte-valued fields: Variable Type Description ar_binary_tag(time, lat, lon) byte Binary AR mask: 1 = atmospheric river, 0 = no atmospheric river ar_type(time, lat, lon) b

title: DARK atmospheric-river tags: IVT q098 threshold (ERA5, 1979–2025)
description: This dataset provides annual global binary atmospheric-river (AR) masks derived from the ERA5 reanalysis using the DARK detection algorithm, formerly Buffet v1.0. It contains 6-hourly output for every year from 1979 to 2025 on the native ERA5 0.25° × 0.25° grid. Although DARK was developed with a polar and Antarctic focus, the algorithm is applied globally. The output follows the ARTMIP Tier-1 data structure for yearly atmospheric-river masks. Scientific reference Please cite the associated methodological paper when using this dataset: Buffet, V., Favier, V., Pohl, B., and Wille, J. D. (2026). Curved atmospheric rivers and their moisture remnants: a new detection tool for Antarctica . Weather and Climate Dynamics , 7, 1189–1210. https://doi.org/10.5194/wcd-7-1189-2026 Input data Integrated Vapor Transport (IVT) is calculated from the ERA5 vertically integrated water-vapour flux components: viwve : vertically integrated eastward water-vapour flux; viwvn : vertically integrated northward water-vapour flux. The input data are 6-hourly ERA5 reanalysis fields. Method Rolling seasonal IVT threshold For each leap day-of-year, from 1 to 366, a 15-day rolling climatology of IVT is calculated. The local 98th-percentile IVT value defines a seasonally varying threshold at every grid cell. The q098 threshold field was calculated from the ERA5 reference period 1979–2025. For non-leap years, dates on and after 29 February are mapped to the corresponding leap-year day-of-year by shifting the day-of-year by one. Exceedance mask A grid cell is initially classified as part of an atmospheric river when its IVT exceeds the local threshold for the corresponding day of the year. Area filtering Candidate AR regions are identified using 8-connected components with periodic longitude boundaries, preserving continuity across the dateline. Components smaller than 200,000 km² are removed. Grid-cell areas are calculated on WGS-84 using the local geocentric radius and latitude–longitude spacing. Length filtering Each connected component is skeletonized and represented as a graph. The endpoint-to-endpoint path best aligned with the component principal axis is selected, extended to the component edges, and smoothed using a B-spline. Sub-grid geodesic segment lengths are calculated on WGS-84. Components shorter than 2,000 km are removed. Files and format One NetCDF file is provided per year: ERA5.ar_tag.DARK.q098.6hourly.YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD.nc Each file contains: Variable Type Description ar_binary_tag(time, lat, lon) byte Binary AR mask: 1 = atmospheric river; 0 = no atmospheric river The yearly files declare the global convention: Conventions = "CF-1.6" The ar_binary_tag variable includes the following attributes: description = "binary indicator of atmospheric river" scheme = "DARK" version = "1.0" credits = "Developed by Victoire Buffet, Vincent Favier, and Benjamin Pohl" area_filter_km2 = 200000 area_filter_type = "toroidal_longitude_component_filter" The time coordinate uses the standard calendar. Latitude and longitude correspond to the global ERA5 grid. Spatial and temporal coverage Spatial coverage: global ERA5 native 0.25° × 0.25° grid. Temporal coverage: 1979–2025. Temporal resolution: 6-hourly. Reference period used for the seasonal q098 threshold: 1979–2025. Main parameters IVT percentile threshold: 98th percentile Rolling climatological window: 15 days Minimum AR area: 200,000 km² Minimum AR length: 2,000 km Connectivity: 8-connected components with periodic longitude boundaries Interpretation This q098 dataset is the DARK reference configuration. Separate datasets using q080, q085, q090, q092, q094, q096, q097, and q099 IVT thresholds are available as sensitivity experiments. Those datasets document the sensitivity of the results to the percentile threshold and should not be interpreted as the official DARK reference configuration. title: DESIGNING AN AI-BASED ONLINE ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEM FOR HIGHER EDUCATION: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL INTEGRATING MULTIDIMENSIONAL LEARNER MODELLING, KNOWLEDGE TRACING AND LMS INTEROPERABILITY
description: Universities increasingly rely on learning management systems (LMS) for online and blended learning, yet these platforms rarely adapt instruction to the individual learner. Existing adaptive solutions are often proprietary, isolated from the institutional LMS, opaque to teachers and unavailable for national-language content. Aim. The article presents a conceptual model of an AI-based online adaptive learning system for higher education that integrates a multidimensional learner model, an interpretable adaptation engine and standards-based interoperability with existing LMS. Methods. The study follows the design science research methodology (Peffers et al., 2007). Design requirements were derived from a review of research on adaptive learning, learner modelling and AI in education, and from strategic documents on the digitalisation of higher education in Uzbekistan. The artefact was then designed and specified, and a plan for its demonstration and evaluation was developed. Results. The model comprises five design principles; a domain model structured around knowledge components; a multidimensional learner model combining cognitive (Bayesian knowledge tracing), behavioural and motivational indicators; an adaptation engine that selects learning activities within the learner's zone of proximal development using item response theory; a layered architecture integrated with the LMS via IMS LTI 1.3 and the Experience API (xAPI); and a teacher dashboard that supports human oversight. An evaluation framework with measurable criteria is proposed. Conclusion. The model offers a transparent and technically feasible basis for introducing adaptive learning into national higher education platforms. Its effectiveness will be tested empirically in a quasi-experimental study. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23386234

title: DONALD TRUMP AND HIS ADMINISTRATION'S POLICIES: IMPACT ON EUROPE AND THE GROWING RUSSIAN INFLUENCE ON THE CONTINENT
description: It can be said that today, Donald Trump’s second administration’s relations with the European Union differ from those of his previous presidency. Moreover, Donald Trump has made “tariff policy” a central part of his political vocabulary, and such a policy has a serious impact on relations between states. In addition, the slogan “America First” takes priority under Trump, and this approach directly and indirectly affects the transatlantic alliance, in particular NATO and the European Union. At the same time, the shift of U.S. political attention from Europe to the regions of Asia and Africa is creating favorable ground for Russia to intensify its political activity in the region. This article analyzes the main foreign policy directions of the Trump administration, their impact on Europe, and, against this background, the factors behind the relative growth of Russian influence in Europe. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23299302

title: DVFS-Aware Piecewise GPU Power Model Parameters for GROMACS, AMBER, and FIRESTARTER on NVIDIA A40, A100, H100, H200 and AMD MI300X
description: This dataset provides fitted parameters of a DVFS-aware piecewise power model that predicts the average GPU board power as a function of the GPU core (graphics) clock for scientific workloads. Model. For each GPU, application, and benchmark, power is modeled as P(f) = b1·f + c1 for f ≤ f_t (linear, leakage-dominated regime) and P(f) = a2·f² + b2·f + c2 for f > f_t (quadratic, voltage-dominated regime), where f is the graphics clock in MHz, P is in watts, and f_t is the fitted transition frequency. In practice, power is capped at the device’s TDP. The coefficients were fitted by nonlinear least squares (Levenberg–Marquardt) to measured steady-state power across frequency sweeps. Coverage. NVIDIA A40, A100, H100, H200: GROMACS benchmarks 1–6 and AMBER benchmarks 1–11 AMD MI300X: FIRESTARTER stress test. Unlike the NVIDIA GPUs, its power scales linearly with clock, so only the linear branch is used. Measurement. Power was read from on-board sensors (nvidia-smi or rocm-smi) every 100 ms and averaged over a steady-state window after thermal stabilization, at fixed memory clocks and the default power limit, with graphics clocks locked per run. Format. DVFS_PARAMS.js is an ES module exporting DVFS_PARAMS[gpu][application][benchmark] = { f_t, b1, c1, a2, b2, c2 } . Units: f_t in MHz; b1 and b2 in W/MHz; a2 in W/MHz²; c1 and c2 in W. Use. The parameters are the preloaded power profiles of the Wattlytics web platform, which performs performance–energy–TCO co-optimization for GPU clusters. They can be used directly for energy estimation and frequency-tuning studies. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23258567

title: Data and code for "Future aerosol absorption undergoes geographical reorganization despite small global changes"
description: Supporting data and code for “Future aerosol absorption undergoes geographical reorganization despite small global changes“. And this dataset also provides a global land aerosol absorption optical depth (AAOD) product for 2018–2024, derived using AMPCN and constrained by observations. It offers daily  AOD (Band 1),SSA(Band 2), and AAOD(Band 3) estimates at 550 nm on a 0.04° × 0.04° grid. AMPCN combines multi-angular, multispectral, and polarimetric observations from GCOM-C/SGLI with ground-based aerosol absorption data and radiative transfer constraints to estimate column-integrated aerosol absorption over land. The record also includes monthly AAOD projections at 550 nm for 2025–2050 under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5 on a 1° × 1° grid. These projections were generated using observation-anchored LightGBM surrogates trained against AMPCN AAOD and driven by CMIP6 predictors from seven climate models representing five modelling families. Final monthly fields were calculated by taking the median within each family and then the median across the five families. The exported variable, aaod, contains absolute, dimensionless AAOD values. Author information is temporarily withheld and will be added when the record is published after peer review. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23485479

title: Data and code for: Leaf photosynthetic capacity and radial growth show no decline toward the northern range boundary of yellow birch
description: This dataset supports the manuscript "Leaf photosynthetic capacity and radial growth show no decline toward the northern range boundary of yellow birch" examining performance of yellow birch ( Betula alleghaniensis ) across a latitudinal gradient at its northern range boundary in western Quebec, Canada. Gas-exchange measurements were collected using a LI-6800 portable photosynthesis system with the Rapid A-Ci Response (RACiR) technique, on excised branches from 150 trees (adults and saplings) across 15 plots. Raw curves were corrected against empty-chamber reference measurements and, for a subset of trees, cleaned of clearly erroneous points through an interactive process; the exact per-curve range and outlier decisions from this step were not logged. Corrected curves are provided as individual CSV files ( data/GasExchange/ ), along with an R script ( data/GasExchange/FitPhotosynthesis.R ) that performs the fully deterministic step of fitting each curve to extract Vc,max and Jmax using the photosynthesis R package. Tree-ring samples were collected via increment cores from 75 adult trees, crossdated, and measured for annual ring width. Ring-width series are provided in standard .rwl format ( data/rwl/ ), one file per plot, together with the CooRecorder coordinate files ( data/POS/ ) used to estimate the years to pith, and bark thickness measurements ( data/YBRB-BarkThickness.csv ) used in basal area increment reconstruction. Plot-level topographic, soil, and vegetation community data are provided as CSV files, along with monthly maximum and minimum temperature and total precipitation for each plot (1942–2022) from Natural Resources Canada’s 60 arc-second gridded climate surfaces (McKenney et al., 2011). scripts/analysis.R documents the full statistical pipeline from these processed data files through to the reported analyses and figure. See README.md for a description of all files and the package versions used. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23536917

title: Data and code for: National monitoring identifies habitat or connectivity priorities for only a minority of freshwater fishes
description: This deposit contains the analysis-ready data, model outputs and code supporting the article "National monitoring identifies habitat or connectivity priorities for only a minority of freshwater fishes" (Journal of Applied Ecology). The study combined South Korea's standardized national fish monitoring (3,400 site-years, 2023–2025, 126 species) with the RiverATLAS river network and a structural-barrier inventory. Species-specific occupancy models were validated on entire river networks withheld from fitting, and Shapley values partitioned the held-out predictive information supplied by local habitat and by structural connectivity. A within-network permutation null and a block-tuned regularization were used to assess chance signals and sensitivity. Contents - code/: all analysis scripts (Python 3.12, run under WSL2/Ubuntu); run order in code/README_CODE.md, package versions in code/requirements_public.txt. - data/analysis_input/: site-year design (predictors, cross-validation fold, river-network component), two-round detection histories, predictor-to-block manifest, species support and FishBase-derived traits. - data/model_output/: held-out log predictive densities and site-year Shapley values for all estimable species, species-level summaries, and outputs of the revision analyses (reclassification, block-tuned regularization, permutation null, figure source data). - supplementary_tables/: Supplementary Tables S1–S11 of the article.   Privacy Monitoring sites and river reaches are identified by pseudonymous codes; coordinates, site names and real reach identifiers are withheld to avoid disclosing locations of protected species. Network topology is preserved through consistent reach codes. Raw survey records and the raw barrier inventory are not redistributed; only the reach-level barrier counts used in the models are included. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23353862

description: This dataset accompanies the article “Crystal-structure design by agentic AI in a language of motifs” (preprint: arXiv:2608.15900). MatEvolve is an agentic-AI framework in which a language model designs crystals by editing motif profiles, text descriptions of the recurring geometric building blocks of a crystal; candidates are validated by density functional theory (DFT). The dataset contains the DFT-validated candidates from the benchmark on rare-earth-lean permanent magnets, in which MatEvolve was compared with MatterGen (unconditioned and magnetization-conditioned) and Chemeleon2 at an equal budget of 400 DFT relaxations per method. For each candidate it reports [chemical formula, space group, formation energy, energy above the convex hull, saturation magnetization μ0Ms, and the stable/unique/novel, magnetic and new-prototype flags used in the article]. Version 1.0 contains the tabular data (CSV) only. The DFT-relaxed crystal structures (CIF) will be added in a later version. title: Data supporting the study: Estimating Urban Interception Evaporation Using a Multi-source Data-driven Model at a Flux Site
description: Urban Reference-based Evaporation Partitioning (UREP), version 2 UREP is a reference-based framework for partitioning urban evaporation into reference evaporation (Ets) and interception evaporation (Ei). This release provides the data, Python code, trained models and results for its application at the Vancouver-Sunset (CA-Sunset) flux-tower site in Canada. The framework combines two models. The Ets model uses a random forest to predict surface conductance, followed by the Penman–Monteith equation to estimate reference evaporation. During dry periods, available energy is calculated from four-component net radiation minus a seasonal OHM-based storage estimate. This formulation avoids constructing the energy input directly from the target latent heat flux, thereby limiting target leakage during reference-model training. The dry-period reference model is subsequently applied during wet periods, using LE + H as the available-energy proxy. This choice reduces sample loss associated with missing four-component radiation measurements and increases the wet-period data available for residual construction and Ei training. Wet-period calculations therefore depend on the availability of LE and H. Positive differences between observed latent heat flux and simulated reference evaporation are attributed to interception evaporation under the reference-based partitioning assumption. A second random forest models these positive residuals using meteorological forcing, wind, surface characteristics, NDVI and causal rainfall features, without an upper residual cutoff. The processing workflow includes time alignment, variable-specific quality control, wet–dry classification using a six-daylight-hour post-rainfall window, rainfall-feature extraction, surface-height and roughness calculations, dynamic flux-footprint weighting, NDVI processing, MOST-based aerodynamic conductance and seasonal storage estimation. Training, validation and test partitions preserve complete rainfall events and dry-period time blocks. Model parameters are selected using validation RMSE of final latent heat flux for Ets and the interception residual for Ei. The archive contains source flux observations, GIS and NDVI data, processed model inputs, complete processing and training scripts, fitted models, calibration records, predictions, evaluation metrics and figures. Documentation specifies model configurations, variable units, data sources and commands for reproducing the workflow. Evaporation outputs are provided as latent heat flux in W m⁻² and equivalent water depth in mm per 30-minute interval. Code and documentation are licensed under MIT, and original processed data under CC BY 4.0. Third-party source datasets retain their respective original terms. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23463259

title: Data underlying the figures of "Twin Tidal Experiments with FESOM2 on a Kilometre-Scale Global Mesh. Part 1: Resolved Internal Tides and a Numerical Ocean Heat Pump"
description: Data plotted in all figures of Sein et al. (submitted to the Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems), "Twin Tidal Experiments with FESOM2 on a Kilometre-Scale Global Mesh. Part 1: Resolved Internal Tides and a Numerical Ocean Heat Pump": main-text Figures 1-15, appendix Figures A1-D1 and Supporting Information Figures S1-S16. The data come from a 37-year twin experiment with the global ocean-sea ice model FESOM2 on a mesh with 30 million surface nodes (about 1 km resolution on shelves, slopes and in straits), with (JON) and without (JOFF) explicit luni-solar tidal forcing, 2001-2015 climatologies, and 2016 runs with 3-hourly output including a tidal switch-off run (JOFFON). One zip archive per figure (netCDF-4/CF and CSV files with a README that maps panels to variables), and the model mesh (jack_mesh_coords.nc) for fields stored on the native mesh. title: Database on high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in albatrosses and petrels (ACAP HPAI)
description: High pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses have rapidly emerged as a major global threat to wildlife, with severe consequences for seabird populations. Albatrosses and petrels (order Procellariiformes) are particularly vulnerable due to their long lifespan, low reproductive rates and strong site fidelity. Since 2021, HPAI viruses have caused unprecedented mortality in seabird communities worldwide and have expanded into the core range of procellariiform species, including sub-Antarctic and Antarctic regions. In response to the urgent need for timely, species-relevant information, the Agreement on the Conservation of Albatrosses and Petrels (ACAP) established the High Pathogenicity H5Nx Avian Influenza Intersessional Correspondence Group (HPAI-ICG), which developed the ACAP HPAI database — an openly accessible, regularly updated resource that consolidates all known suspected and confirmed HPAI events involving procellariiform birds. The database compiles information from global and national reporting systems, scientific literature, genetic repositories, government communications and direct expert notifications. Events are standardised using transparent case definitions, cross-referenced and validated by subject-matter experts and complemented by additional data on case impacts and viral characteristics. The database provides a critical decision-support tool for governments, researchers, conservation practitioners and tourism operators, contributing to the planning and implementation of HPAI biosafety, surveillance, monitoring and outbreak response activities. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23341415

description: This dataset documents occurrences of the contemporary English expression 'X likey', including the alternative spellings 'likey', 'likee', 'likie' and 'like-y', examined in Rodríguez-Abruñeiras (2022). title: Dataset and code: Experimental evidence for intergenerational effects of a contaminated and low-quality diet in a long-lived seabird
description: Abstract of the study: Marine organisms are experiencing unprecedented selective pressures from multiple anthropogenic stressors, including chemical pollution and associated changes in prey quality. As top predators, seabirds are exposed to these pressures. While the direct impacts of contaminants and low food quality on seabirds are relatively well documented, far less is known about their potential intergenerational effects on offspring morphology and physiology. Yet, filling this gap is crucial, as early-life development can have lasting consequences on individual fitness. Using a novel experimental setting, we fed breeding Common gulls (Larus canus) with either fish originating from polluted or clean habitats during the egg-laying period. Fish caught from the polluted habitat were confirmed to contain higher concentrations of a cocktail of non-essential trace elements and a lower energy content compared to fish from the clean habitat. Chicks from parents exposed to lower-quality and more contaminated food hatched with smaller head-bill lengths and tended to exhibit lower hatchling mass when parents were fed fish from the polluted habitat during egg formation. Moreover, these chicks exhibited lower baseline corticosterone and an altered relationship between growth and corticosterone compared to chicks from parents fed with fish from the clean habitat. Although the relative contribution of contaminant exposure and prey quality cannot be disentangled in the present design, our study provides rare experimental evidence that an environmentally relevant compound stressor can generate negative intergenerational effects in seabirds. Our findings highlight a pathway through which human-driven environmental changes may alter early-life development and, consequently, population dynamics in wild marine vertebrates. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23396047

Dataset for: Small-scale mixing regulates the reconfiguration of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone
description: This repository contains the processed dataset used in the study “Small-scale mixing regulates the reconfiguration of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone.” The data are derived from SeaExplorer glider observations collected in the northwestern Arabian Sea and Sea of Oman between November 2024 and February 2025. The dataset includes the hydrographic, dissolved oxygen, current velocity, and microstructure turbulence variables used in the analyses and figures presented in the manuscript. It contains quality-controlled and gridded observations, derived seawater properties, processed AD2CP velocity fields, and microstructure-based estimates of turbulent kinetic energy and temperature-variance dissipation rates. Each variable within the NetCDF file has its corresponding attributes and metadata. These data were used to quantify distinct oxygen supply pathways, characterize small-scale mixing regimes, estimate diapycnal oxygen fluxes and flux convergence, and assess how mixing redistributes oxygen across different oxygen classes within the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone. The original observational data are archived separately on Zenodo. This repository provides the processed data products used for the manuscript analysis. The analysis and figure-generation code required to reproduce the results will be made available through the associated GitHub repository.  DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22650492

title: Dataset for: Understanding methane cleavage on medium-entropy oxides
description: This dataset accompanies the article "Understanding methane cleavage on medium-entropy oxides" by S. Yuan, H. Song, Z. Wu and D.-e. Jiang (Catalysis Science & Technology, 2026). It provides site-resolved, DFT-computed adsorption energies and climbing-image nudged-elastic-band (CI-NEB) activation barriers for the first C-H bond cleavage of methane (CH4 -> CH3 + H) on the (100) surface of a medium-entropy oxide, the equimolar quaternary oxide Mg0.25Ni0.25Cu0.25Zn0.25O. Version 2 adds the slab, adsorption and CI-NEB structures, the VASP input files, and the script and output files of the SISSO descriptor analysis, so that every number in the article can be traced to a structure and the machine-learning analysis can be reproduced directly. CONTENTS activation.csv - 77 elementary C-H cleavage reactions (30 heterolytic, 21 homolytic-trans, 26 homolytic-cis), in 9 columns: a reaction identifier, the mechanism, the site indices and identities of the CH4-, CH3- and H-hosting sites, and the CI-NEB activation energy Ea. site_adsorption_energies.csv - single-fragment adsorption energies of H, CH3 and CH4 at each of the 16 lattice sites of the MEO (100) cell (8 metal-cation sites and 8 lattice-oxygen sites, indexed 1-16). These site indices are the same indices used in the reaction identifiers, so the per-site adsorption energies can be attached to any reaction by joining on the site index. SISSO_features_12.csv - the mechanism-free 12-feature table (77 rows) that is the input to the SISSO activation-energy descriptor reported in the article (Section 3.3). It contains only continuous electronic-structure and adsorption descriptors; the mechanism label can be recovered from activation.csv via the reaction id. slab/ - the clean five-layer 4x4 Mg0.25Ni0.25Cu0.25Zn0.25O(100) slab (clean_slab.vasp) with its INCAR and KPOINTS, and site_index_map.csv, which links the site indices 1-16 to the atom index in clean_slab.vasp and, for oxygen sites, to the subsurface cation directly beneath. adsorption/ - relaxed single-fragment adsorption structures of CH4, CH3 and H at each of the 16 sites (adsorption/<CH4|CH3|H>/<site index>_<site element>.vasp) with the shared INCAR and KPOINTS. neb/<i_j_k>/ - one folder per reaction: the full CI-NEB band of six images (image_00 to image_05, i.e. two end points plus four intermediate images), the initial state IS.vasp, the highest-energy image TS.vasp, the final state FS.vasp, and the INCAR and KPOINTS actually used. neb_manifest.csv lists, for every reaction, the mechanism, the published Ea and the index of the TS image. sisso/ - run_sisso.py (self-contained Python script reproducing Eq. (1) of the article and all validation statistics), descriptor_selection.csv (descriptors selected at dimension 1-4), validation_summary.csv (full fit, leave-one-out, nested leave-one-out and grouped cross-validation), loocv_predictions.csv (per-reaction predictions behind the parity plot) and README_sisso.txt describing the protocol. README_structures.txt - description of the structure, input and SISSO folders, including the PAW datasets used. SITE-NAMING SCHEME Each reaction is identified by a three-number code i_j_k: i is the cation site on which CH4 is adsorbed, j is the site that hosts the CH3 fragment after cleavage, and k is the lattice-oxygen site that hosts the abstracted H atom. For heterolytic cleavage the CH3 group remains on the original cation (j = i); for the homolytic pathways j and k are both lattice-oxygen sites, and "trans"/"cis" denote their relative geometry around the cation. COLUMN DEFINITIONS - activation.csv reaction_id: reaction identifier i_j_k. mechanism: heterolytic, homolytic_trans or homolytic_cis. ch4_cation_idx / ch4_cation: index and element of the cation i on which CH4 adsorbs. ch3_site_idx / ch3_site: index and identity of the site j hosting CH3. h_site_idx / h_site: index and identity of the lattice oxygen k hosting H. Ea_eV: CI-NEB activation energy (eV). COLUMN D

title: Declaring Worldviews in SSM for Sustainability & Community Learning
description: Declaring Worldviews in SSM for Sustainability & Community Learning Systemic Practice and Action Research , Volume 39, article number 2 (2026)   Abstract For over fifty years, Soft Systems ideas and the Soft Systems Methodology (SSM) have played a pivotal role in understanding various problem situations and initiating action. Often tackling the grandest challenges of our time, SSM will retain continued relevance in helping decision-makers address sustainability challenges within organisations and their communities. In this paper, we are concerned with the meaningful co-creation of sustainable value through community-based learning using SSM. More specifically, recognising that a sustainability paradigm, characterised by the need to create a just and safe space for humanity to thrive within the means of a living planet (as called for by Raworth, 2017), is often marginalised or overlooked. This paradigm presents us with an ethical imperative, complex and messy challenges/issues, and a set of ideals (articulated in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals) that are significantly off track. This paper employs a variation of the Delphi method, drawing on the authors’ collective interest and experience in applying SSM in communities, to propose a double-loop learning cycle to explore the underlying assumptions of our worldviews and mental models within communities. We suggest that an SSM learning cycle can be enhanced by initiating conversations on relevant models for sustainability (such as Doughnut Economics, UN SDGs, and the principles for a Circular Economy), to find common ground for triggering new learning. This idea is contextualised and proposed as the value(s)-action gap phenomenon, which can help explain the difference between an individual, an organisation, and/or a community's intention(s) and their actual action(s). In doing so, find common ground, shift to higher levels of systems consciousness from an ego-centric to an ecosystem level of awareness, engage communities, and take an intergenerational perspective. We suggest that incorporating a double-loop learning cycle into SSM can support organisations and their communities in putting shared values into meaningful action. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23589411

title: Drowning in a sandy ocean: Epiarenic growth of Tillandsia in the hyperarid Atacama Desert
description: The Atacama Desert hosts a unique ecosystem formed by the sand-dwelling and rootless Tillandsia landbeckii known as Tillandsia lomas or tillandsiales, which extends over hundreds of square kilometers. Although fog provides its primary water source, the role of aeolian sand in the persistence and spatial structure of these populations remains insufficiently studied and understood. We compared three populations in northern, central, and southern parts of the Chilean Atacama Desert (Arica, Oyarbide, and Caldera), combining wind observations, terrain data, vegetation structure, population-genomic data with substrate properties. The study draws on records from six climate stations, 1246 substrate samples, genomic data from 545 individuals, satellite imagery, and digital terrain models. Our findings demonstrate that regional wind regimes provide a mechanism for transporting sand into the study areas, whereas lower wind velocities within the vegetation favour local sand deposition but less abrasion and burial. Across the three populations, vegetated sites had moderately sorted sandy substrates, while sites with sparse or dead vegetation differed in substrate characteristics and often revealed finer grain sizes and higher sortation indices (more poorly sorted substrate). Genomic analyses revealed pronounced spatial genetic structure alongside an excess of heterozygosity, which is maintained by vegetative reproduction, clonal growth and dispersal. Genetic spatial structures follow topographic features and wind system characteristics such as wind speed and direction. Together, these results show that T. landbeckii is associated with a distinctive balance between regional sand transport and local sand retention. Our results support the view that aeolian sand is not merely a substrate but an integral component of the physical environment in which these fog-dependent populations persist and changes in wind systems will not only alter fog deposition, but may also have a direct effect on plant stability, growth dynamics and vegetation integrity. The herein described fine-scaled interdependencies of biotic and abiotic parameters shaping T. landbeckii populations and vegetation integrity also shed some light on major future threats eventually even enhancing present-day landscape-level dieback.   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23389709

title: Dystopia, anti-utopia, genre evolution, concept of the future, comparative literature, technocracy, totalitarianism, national identity, ecological degradation.
description: This article provides a comparative-typological study of the artistic interpretation of the future concept and the evolutionary features of the dystopian genre in 21st-century English and Uzbek literature. Unlike classical 20th-century anti-utopias, modern dystopian prose reflects how global technological networking, artificial intelligence, ecological crises, and information manipulation have transformed the imagery of the future. The research comparatively analyzes that while English dystopian literature predominantly emphasizes technological determinism and post-humanism, modern Uzbek dystopia centers on the preservation of national identity, moral-ethical values, and historical memory. The research findings serve as a valuable theoretical resource for comparative literary studies and the analysis of contemporary literary processes. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23303304

title: ENBLOC: Input Data for an LLM-Based Agent-Based Model of Collective Decision-Making on Photovoltaic Investments in Housing Cooperatives
description: This dataset contains the input data and model parameters for the LLM-based agent-based model (LLM-ABM) developed within the ENBLOC research project to investigate collective decision-making on photovoltaic (PV) investments in housing cooperatives in Czechia and Poland. The dataset includes two country-specific input configurations, each representing a residential building with 30 agents (one agent per apartment). For each country, the materials include: Agent database (database.xlsx): Individual-level characteristics and attitudes used to construct resident agents, including sociodemographic characteristics, housing tenure, environmental and technological attitudes, community relationships, trust, and participation in collective decision-making. Building characteristics (building.xlsx): Technical and structural parameters of the modelled residential building. Photovoltaic project parameters (project.xlsx): Technical and financial assumptions defining the photovoltaic investment scenario. Variable key (variable key for database.xlsx): Definitions and coding schemes for the agent-level variables. The Czech and Polish configurations enable the application of the same modelling framework in two national contexts. The dataset accompanies the ENBLOC LLM-ABM software and supports the transparency and reproducibility of the simulations investigating collective investment decision-making in multi-family housing. title: Experimental Small-Angle X-Ray Scattering (SAXS) and Viscosity Data for Concentrated siRNA Up to 350 mg/mL
description: This collection contains experimental small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) data files for concentrated siRNA up to 350 mg/mL in water (no added salt) and with 150mM added NaCl. Experimental viscosities were also recorded at 20C for siRNA in water. The siRNA is proprietary 59-nt self-complimentary duplex with a GalNAc ligand. The ligand was conjugated to the hairpin loop of the duplex. Backbone modifications were applied to each residue. The SAXS data was collected using the ID-7A1 high pressure beamline at the Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source (CHESS). Viscosity data was collected at Eli Lilly and Co. The authors would like to thank Eli Lilly and Co. for providing funding, siRNA material and the experimental scattering and viscosity data.  This work is based on research conducted at the Center for High-Energy X-ray Sciences (CHEXS), which is supported by the National Science Foundation (BIO, ENG and MPS Directorates) under award DMR-2342336, and the Macromolecular Diffraction at CHESS (MacCHESS) facility, which is supported by award 1-P30-GM124166 from the National Institute of General Medical Sciences and the National Institutes of Health.
