title: Experimental dataset on the mix design and mechanical performance of thin and ultra-thin asphalt mixtures incorporating RAP, steel slag and ceramic waste
description: Dataset description This dataset contains experimental data obtained during the design and mechanical characterisation of thin (BBTM 11B) and ultra-thin (AUTL 11) asphalt mixtures incorporating high proportions of recovered materials for potential application in bike lanes. The mixtures were manufactured using reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) combined with either steel slag aggregates (SSA) or ceramic waste aggregates (CWA). Mixture identification and dosage nomenclature Each asphalt mixture is identified by its mixture type (AUTL 11 or BBTM 11B) and a dosage code indicating the proportions of recovered materials. The dosage code follows the format RxxSyy or RxxCyy, where R denotes reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP), S denotes steel slag aggregates (SSA), and C denotes ceramic waste aggregates (CWA). The numbers indicate the corresponding percentages by mass of the aggregate blend. For example, R65S35 represents a mixture containing 65% RAP and 35% SSA, whereas R35C65 represents a mixture containing 35% RAP and 65% CWA. The percentages in each dosage code sum to 100% and do not represent the bitumen content, which is reported separately. The dataset is organised into two Microsoft Excel files: 1. Optimum_content_bitumen.xlsx This file contains the experimental data used to determine the optimum bitumen content for each asphalt mixture formulation. Individual specimen measurements are provided for each mixture type and aggregate composition, considering five bitumen contents per formulation. The recorded variables include: Maximum density (g/cm³), determined according to UNE-EN 12697-5. Bulk density (g/cm³), determined according to UNE-EN 12697-6. Air void content (%), determined according to UNE-EN 12697-8. Particle loss (%), determined according to UNE-EN 12697-17. These measurements provide the experimental basis for evaluating the volumetric characteristics and particle loss resistance of the investigated mixtures at different bitumen contents. 2. Tests_results.xlsx This file contains the mechanical characterisation results obtained for asphalt mixtures manufactured at their selected optimum bitumen contents. Unlike the first file, which includes measurements at five bitumen contents, all results in this workbook correspond exclusively to the optimum bitumen content selected for each formulation. The workbook comprises four worksheets: Water sensitivity: Results of the water sensitivity test conducted according to UNE-EN 12697-12, including indirect tensile strength measurements under dry and wet conditioning and the corresponding indirect tensile strength ratio (ITSR). Permanent deformation: Results of the wheel tracking test conducted according to UNE-EN 12697-22, including wheel tracking slope (WTS), proportional rut depth (PRD), and rut depth (RD). Stiffness: Results of the stiffness test conducted according to UNE-EN 12697-26, including stiffness modulus measurements. Cracking: Results of the Fénix test conducted according to NLT-383/25 at three temperatures (20, 5, and −5 °C), including tensile strength, ductility, fracture-related energy parameters, and approximate toughness. Each worksheet identifies the asphalt mixture type, aggregate composition, and bitumen content, allowing the experimental results to be associated with their corresponding formulations. Testing standards The experimental procedures followed the standards listed below: UNE-EN 12697-5:2020. Bituminous Mixtures — Test Methods — Part 5: Determination of the Maximum Density. UNE-EN 12697-6:2012. Bituminous Mixtures — Test Methods for Hot Mix Asphalt — Part 6: Determination of Bulk Density of Bituminous Specimens. UNE-EN 12697-8:2020. Bituminous Mixtures — Test Methods — Part 8: Determination of Void Characteristics of Bituminous Specimens. UNE-EN 12697-17:2018. Bituminous Mixtures — Test Methods — Part 17: Particle Loss of Porous Asphalt Specimens. UNE-EN 12697-12:2019. Bitumino

title: FAIR²-FoodHealth: a provenance-rich knowledge graph linking empirical food composition, nutrients, health-variable definitions and cardiometabolic guidance
description: Background: Food, nutrition and health data differ in terminology, identifiers, units and access conditions, so joining them by name or code can silently attach evidence to the wrong concept. Methods: FAIR²-FoodHealth publishes tidy CSV tables and an RDF knowledge graph generated deterministically from them, preserving source-native terms and values. Links to FoodOn, ChEBI, the NCI Thesaurus, LOINC and the Mondo Disease Ontology are qualified SKOS mappings with method, confidence, review status and licence; and hypertension, obesity and type 2 diabetes are linked to the nutrients on which cited dietary guidance focuses, with locators and populations. An empirical layer from USDA FoodData Central contributes 52 food records from two releases with 398 per-100 g values copied unchanged, and 20 computationally drafted source-nutrient decisions, including explicit rejections of total sugars as added sugars and of food energy content as energy intake. Results: Version 0.4.0 comprises 24 tables (666 records) and 15,028 triples; the tables, SHACL shapes, a complete CSV-to-RDF round trip, pinned queries for eleven competency questions and 45 tests (34 injected defects) all pass. Qualified mapping yields 196 value-to-guideline paths for 28 Foundation Foods records; a naive shared-word join yields 434, of which 238 attach added-sugar or energy-intake guidance to the wrong quantity. Exact description matching linked 18 of 24 same-food records without error, whereas token similarity proposed 3 wrong links. Conclusions: Food scientists can use the tidy CSV tables directly for federated analytics, data-quality checks and cross-release compositional comparisons in which every link is a recorded decision rather than a silent name match. Digital-health developers and AI engineers can deploy the RDF graph and qualified mappings to ground retrieval-augmented nutrition assistants in cited, provenance-rich evidence instead of fragile string matching. All mapping and matching decisions are computational drafts awaiting independent expert-panel review; the checks establish structural integrity, not nutritional or clinical validity, and FAIR² compliance is not claimed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23394326

title: FREE-ION GROUND STATE, EFFECTIVE AXIAL CRYSTAL FIELD AND SINGLE-ION MAGNETOTHERMAL PROPERTIES OF THE Dy3+ ION IN ORTHOALUMINATE DyAlO3
description: Abstract.  The Dy 3+  ion in dysprosium orthoaluminate DyAlO 3  is a Kramers ion with one of the largest magnetic moments in the lanthanide series, but its single-ion properties have mostly been described qualitatively. This work builds a quantitative chain from free-ion theory to measurable thermodynamic quantities. Hund’s rules and LS coupling give the ground term 6 H 15/2 , the Landé factor g J  = 4/3 and the effective moment μ eff  = 10.65 μ B , the highest among the trivalent lanthanides. The energies of the four lowest Kramers doublets of 6 H 15/2  (0, 53.7, 125.7 and 205.5 cm −1 ), obtained from the Stark structure of the 6 H 15/2   → 6 F 3/2  absorption band, were fitted with an effective axial crystal-field Hamiltonian in Stevens operators. A second-order term alone (B 2 0  = −1.75 cm −1 ) leaves an rms deviation of 16.1 cm −1 . Adding the fourth-order term (B 2 0  = −2.55 cm −1 , B 4 0  = 2.45×10 −3  cm −1 ) reduces it to 0.24 cm −1 , confirms the |±15/2⟩ ground doublet and places the four unresolved doublets at 281–416 cm −1 . From this level scheme, the Schottky heat capacity, the magnetic entropy and the magnetization were calculated. The heat-capacity maximum shifts from 57 K (four resolved doublets) to 118 K (complete scheme), which offers a direct calorimetric test of the predicted upper levels. At 10 K and 1 T the Ising doublet gives 5.87 μ B  along its axis, compared with 2.46 μ B  for a free ion and 2.06 μ B  for a powder average. The results provide a consistent single-ion basis for interpreting the magnetic anisotropy and the magnetocaloric potential of DyAlO 3 . DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23243713

title: FROM AGROECOTOURISM TO SPELEOTOURISM: OPPORTUNITIES FOR DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED TOURISM PRODUCT IN SENTOB VILLAGE
description: This article examines opportunities for developing an integrated tourism product in Sentob village by connecting agroecotourism with potential speleotourism experiences. It considers how agricultural activities, rural hospitality, local cultural practices, and nature-based excursions could be combined with cave-related educational or adventure activities where suitable underground resources are verified. A qualitative, desk-based approach is proposed to assess product complementarity, community participation, accessibility, environmental conservation, visitor safety, and service coordination. Particular attention is given to the feasibility of linking accommodation, local food, farm experiences, walking routes, and professionally guided cave visits within a coherent itinerary. The article outlines development priorities, including resource inventories, site-specific assessments, guide training, cooperation among local service providers, and controlled pilot tours. It emphasizes that speleotourism integration requires evidence of accessible and suitable cave sites, together with appropriate conservation and safety arrangements. The proposed framework seeks to support diversified visitor experiences and local economic participation while preserving rural identity and natural heritage. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23277756

title: FUNCTIONAL AND PRAGMATIC FEATURES OF ANAPHORIC DEVICES IN RUSSIAN AND UZBEK PROVERBS
description: The article examines the functional and pragmatic properties of anaphoric devices in Russian and Uzbek proverbs from a comparative perspective. The term anaphora is used primarily in its referential and cohesive sense: an anaphoric expression is interpreted through a previously activated or structurally correlated element, while stylistic initial repetition is considered only when it contributes to referential continuity or pragmatic parallelism. The study focuses on pronominal and correlative constructions, demonstrative and locative reference, reflexive and possessive anaphora, lexical recurrence, and zero or elliptical anaphora. The analysis demonstrates that proverbial discourse makes especially productive use of compact correlation patterns such as Russian kto – tot, chto – to, gde – tam and Uzbek kim – u/o‘sha, nima – shu/shuni, qayerda – shu/o‘sha yerda. These patterns perform more than a cohesive function: they generalize the referent, convert an individual situation into a rule, intensify didactic force, organize cause–effect relations, and reduce the need for explicit nomination. Uzbek proverbs additionally exploit pro-drop and morphologically recoverable reference more freely, whereas Russian examples more often retain overt correlates for structural balance and rhythmic symmetry. The article argues that anaphoric devices constitute one of the mechanisms by which paremias achieve semantic compression, memorability, inferential economy and pragmatic universality. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23490140

title: Global multi-year average soil loss rate during 1960-1990, 1990-2020 and 2080-2100
description: This dataset with 2.5 arc-minutes resolution (approximately 4 km × 4 km) provides global multi-year average soil loss rates calculated using the RUSLE method. The time periods covered are 1960–1990, 1990–2020 and 2080–2100 (under three scenarios). The LS factor was calculated using global 30 m DEM data, and all factors were interpolated to a spatial resolution of 2.5 arc-minutes. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23355150

title: Grain-Scale Radiation Transport and the Robustness of Radiolytic H₂–Sulfate Imbalance in the Revell Crystalline-Rock System
description: This reproducibility package accompanies the study “Grain-Scale Radiation Transport and the Robustness of Radiolytic H₂–Sulfate Imbalance in the Revell Crystalline-Rock System.” The study evaluates how radiation-specific grain-scale transport modifies radiolytic H₂ and sulfate production estimates in the low-porosity Revell crystalline-rock system and tests the robustness of the inferred H₂–sulfate production imbalance. The package contains processed and derived data, analysis and transport-model code, computational notebooks, source data for the main figures, frozen manuscript-level results, and reproducibility metadata. Grain-scale α- and β-radiation transport is evaluated over a grain-diameter sensitivity domain of 0.06–2000 μm, while γ transport and post-interface energy partitioning are treated through explicit sensitivity bounds. The package supports reproduction and audit of the numerical results and figures reported in the associated manuscript. Third-party source datasets are not redistributed as original research data in this archive. Their provenance, persistent identifiers, and access information are documented so that the computational workflow can be traced to the original sources. Research-generated data, figures, and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0, while original research code in the package is released under the MIT License. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23459461

title: Granular matter as a measurable model system for macroscopic state evolution: a transition-centred perspective
description: Granular matter as a measurable model system for macroscopic state evolution: a transition-centred perspective Highlights ·          Five analytical descriptors organize granular state evolution around transitions. ·          Admissible trajectories are distinguished from the realized pathway. ·          Rearrangement cost links path-dependent mechanical work and dissipation. ·          Experiments and DEM connect internal structure with macroscopic regime change. ·          Self-gravitating granular bodies provide the strongest physical extension. Granular matter provides an experimentally accessible system for studying how macroscopic behaviour emerges from constrained rearrangement in discrete many-particle assemblies. Quantities such as the angle of internal friction, dilatancy, particle rearrangement, relaxation, and flow onset are often treated as related but partly separate descriptors of shear response. In this article, we argue that they can be interpreted as coupled manifestations of macroscopic state evolution. We propose a review-based framework organized around five concepts: configuration space, admissible trajectories, rearrangement cost, relaxation pathway, and metastability or regime boundary. Rather than introducing new state variables or a new theory of jamming, the contribution lies in assigning distinct analytical roles to five established concepts and in mapping measurable experimental and discrete element method (DEM) resolved observables onto these roles within a common transition-centred description. The framework links measurable quantities from shear experiments, bulk-solids characterization, and DEM simulations to the evolution of particulate systems between stable, metastable, yielding, and flowing regimes. Its purpose is not to introduce a universal constitutive law, but to provide a physically grounded vocabulary for describing how granular assemblies lose stability, reorganize their internal structure, dissipate energy, and enter new modes of motion. The strongest extension of this framework concerns self-gravitating granular bodies, such as rubble-pile asteroids and regolith-dominated aggregates, where contact mechanics, friction, porosity, and rearrangement remain physically relevant. Broader comparisons with planetary, stellar, or galactic systems are treated only as weaker organizational analogies and are used to clarify the limits of transferability. We therefore identify granular matter as a measurable model system for particulate state evolution and as a reference system for cautious comparison with related discrete many-body systems. title: Hydrodynamically adaptive bioinspired pile arrays for nature-based coastal protection: A numerical study
description: Nature-based and bioinspired solutions are increasingly explored as sustainable alternatives to conventional hard coastal defenses, particularly where maintaining hydrodynamic exchange and water quality is a key requirement. The primary objective of this study is to investigate low-crested pile-based coastal barriers designed to exhibit high permeability under calm wave conditions, while progressively enhancing wave attenuation as meteo-marine forcing increases. Three-dimensional CFD simulations are conducted to analyze wave–structure interaction using a volume-of-fluid approach. Starting from a circular cylindrical pile as a benchmark, we comparatively investigate alternative pile shapes inspired by aquatic flora and fauna. Performance is assessed in terms of wave transmission, reflection, and dissipation coefficients. The results reveal a nonlinear and forcing-dependent response in wave transmission. Under low-energy wave conditions, several configurations exhibit wave transmission coefficients comparable to those of cylindrical piles, promoting flow exchange and limiting stagnation. As wave energy increases, selected bioinspired geometries enhance wave energy dissipation and reduce transmission. A best-performing design, termed r-Biowave, emerged among the others, suggesting that bioinspired pile arrays can function as adaptive coastal protection systems. Therefore, this study provides guidance for selecting the optimal shape of this type of coastal protection under varying wave climates, considering the trade-off between water circulation and storm protection. title: Imperial College 2026 — reGELerate: HyFiP-LDF coarse-grained ratio-sweep simulations (run records, analyses and binding-event replicas)
description: Run records, logs, analyses and binding-event replica trajectories of the streptavidin : fibril ratio sweep simulated by Team Imperial College (iGEM 2026, Imperial College London) with HyFiP-LDF, our open-source coarse-grained HOOMD-blue 7.2.0 Langevin-dynamics model of a protein hydrogel (HET-s(218–289) amyloid fibrils end-labelled with maleimide–PEG–biotin linkers and crosslinked by streptavidin tetramers). The sweep covers six streptavidin : fibril ratios (1/6, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 3) at three random seeds each, 105 ns per run at surrogate conditions (75 nm fibrils, ten times the wet-lab number density, friction scaled by 0.1, 300 nm periodic box), run on one NVIDIA RTX 5090. 13 of 18 runs finished; the configurations and partial logs of the 5 stopped runs are included. Also included are the 52 re-simulations of one binding event (restarted from saved frames with new random seeds at 2 ps resolution) used to study how a biotin finds a streptavidin pocket. For every run: the complete resolved configuration, a run manifest with software versions and every model parameter with its provenance and data-file hashes, the HOOMD energy and temperature log, and the network, thermodynamic and structural analyses. These are the data behind Figures 26–28 and Videos 4–5 of the Simulations page of our wiki. Software: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/imperial-college/cg-langevin-simulation (Apache-2.0). Atomistic reference data: 10.5281/zenodo.23420371. See README.md inside the archive for the file layout, variables, units and methods. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23495176

title: Imperial College 2026: reGELerate: all-atom MD trajectories of a capped HET-s fibril with attached and free Cys–maleimide–PEG12–biotin
description: All-atom molecular dynamics trajectories made by Team Imperial College, iGEM 2026 (Imperial College London) as reference data for a coarse-grained model of a functionalised amyloid fibril, fitted with multi-state iterative Boltzmann inversion (MS-IBI). The system is an 11-chain HET-s(218–289) fibril with an engineered cap docked on one end, carrying the non-canonical residue CYL (cysteine–maleimide–PEG12–biotin). Four simulations: the capped fibril alone in water (150 ns); one capped CYL in water (1 ns); the fibril with CYL attached at two sites (200 ns); the fibril among 40 free capped CYL molecules (200 ns). Amber ff19SB, GAFF2, OPC water, 298 K, GROMACS 2026.3. Solute-only trajectories are included (the full-system trajectories with water and ions are too large and are available on request), with every run's GROMACS input, topology, energy and log files. README.md describes every file, how the runs were set up, how to read them, and their known limitations. Code: NCAA-protein-toolbox on iGEM GitLab . Wiki: https://2026.igem.wiki/imperial-college/. Contact: Harvey Fung, harveyfunghf@gmail.com. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23420371

title: Jacksonville, North Carolina, testbed: hurricane damage and restoration of transmission lines
description: A demonstration, on a real network, of how hurricane wind fields, fragility functions and repair times combine into the failure probability of transmission lines and the time to restore them. It covers the four 230 kV lines that bring power into Jacksonville Substation, North Carolina (750 structures), for Hurricanes Florence (2018), Dorian (2019) and Isaias (2020), three stronger hypothetical storms based on Florence, and four mitigation scenarios. The record includes the network data derived from OpenStreetMap, the results for every storm, scenario and structure, the MATLAB code that reproduces them with the wind fields of the companion record, and a report that explains the method, the inputs and the results. It was produced for the Atlantic Marine Energy Center (AMEC). Network data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23400018

title: Koehler screening of intermetallic superlattices — dataset, calculations and code (v3.0)
description: Dataset, calculations and code supporting the manuscript “Candidate Intermetallic Superlattices for Koehler-Strengthening Experiments: Elastic Contrast, Orientation-Resolved Lattice Matching and Interfacial Stability” (H. Aourag). Main result: a three-filter screening (shear-modulus contrast, orientation-resolved coincidence-lattice matching, interfacial reactivity) of the 16 B2/C11b disilicide pairs. The most contrasted pairs (WSi2 or MoSi2 with AgY, MgY, AgSc or CoTi) react strongly with the disilicide and are rejected. Six aluminide pairs pass all filters; WSi2/NiAl and MoSi2/NiAl are proposed for a first experimental test of the Koehler contribution, with WSi2/CoAl as a weakly contrasted control. Compared for the same orientation and slip variant (resolved moduli and anisotropic Barnett–Lothe energy factors), the reactive pairs reach at most about 10% more maximum estimated image stress than the NiAl pairs, and the control has a 1.1–1.5 times smaller estimated image stress. 44-atom DFT superlattices (commensurate √5×√5/2×2 coincidence cells) give works of separation of 4.43–4.46 J/m² and interface energies of 2.14–2.21 J/m² for the NiAl pairs (2.15 J/m² for a second lateral registry of WSi2/NiAl), and 5.01 and 2.39 J/m² for the control. What is new in v3.0: WSi2/CoAl control superlattice (Quantum ESPRESSO input/output, CIF, interface energies); second lateral registry and k-point test of WSi2/NiAl; like-for-like image-stress estimates per slip variant (variants_v3.py); resolved contrasts of CoTi, AgY and MgY (resolved_others.py); {100}⟨001⟩ slip data; updated figures 6 and 7 with their scripts; complete archive of the Colab interface calculations (QE_interfaces_Colab.tar.gz); updated manifest. Contents: elastic dataset with Materials Project identifiers and acceptance criteria; Quantum ESPRESSO 6.7 and 7.6 input/output files; Python scripts for ranking, slip-system-resolved contrast, energy factors, coherency, lattice matching, reactivity and figures; Google Colab notebooks; relaxed superlattice structures (CIF); a manifest mapping every table and figure of the article to its files (README.md). DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23637270

title: LOCAL AND CENTRALIZED WATER SUPPLY: DRINKING WATER SAFETY AS AN IMPORTANT FACTOR OF PUBLIC HEALTH
description: ABSTRACT : This article describes the content, operating principles, advantages and limitations of centralized and local (decentralized) systems for supplying the population with drinking water. Special attention is paid to the choice of the water source, treatment and disinfection, maintenance of the distribution network, sanitary control and safety measures at the household level. The analysis is based on international guidance on drinking-water quality and small-community water safety, national water legislation and hygienic literature. It is shown that centralized systems allow water to be prepared in a single technological process and to be controlled regularly in the laboratory, but depend on pipes, pumps and a continuous energy supply, whereas local sources such as wells and springs are valuable where the central network does not reach, but their safety depends directly on location, construction, technical condition and the hygienic habits of users. Neither system can be considered superior in all situations: the choice depends on local conditions, water quality, the number of consumers and the possibility of safe management. Safe water is not merely water that looks clean; it is water controlled at all stages from the source to the consumer, protected from contamination and meeting the established quality requirements. The responsibility for this is shared by state bodies, water supply organizations, local communities and each household. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23491711

title: Large-scale characterization of stable water isotopes of cryosphere and hydrological components in glacierized catchments
description: The database compiled in this study represents the first global, harmonized collection of stable water isotope (SWI) measurements across cryosphere and hydrological endmembers in glacierized catchments. It contains 12,348 individual records sourced from 49 peer‑reviewed publications, as well as unpublished datasets contributed directly by the authors. The temporal coverage spans from 1981 to 2023, ensuring both historical and contemporary representation of isotopic conditions in glacier environments. Each entry in the database is described by 44 standardized fields, grouped into four main categories: Bibliographic metadata – data owner, publication year, citation, and publication status. Geographical metadata – continent, country, catchment, glacier name, basin, and coordinates. Sampling details – sample type,sampling period, elevation, and remarks. Isotope data – δ¹⁸O, δ²H, d‑excess, analytical method, measurement error, and uncertainty.  The database integrates Cryosphere and hydrological endmembers, covering precipitation (solid and liquid), snowpack melt, glacier meltwater, glacier ice, supraglacial meltwater, talus‑slope water, rock‑glacier outflow, groundwater, lakes, firn, permafrost thaw, and ice‑cored moraine meltwater.  The stable water isotopes data was generated primarily using CRDS (7,733 δ¹⁸O measurements), IRMS (2,702), OA-ICOS (418) with mean uncertainties of 0.13‰ for δ¹⁸O and 0.49‰ for δ²H.  Geographically, the records span six continents and 20 countries, with strong representation in Europe (5,899 records), Asia (3,132), and North America (3,022), and smaller datasets from South America, Africa, and Oceania. Study locations predominantly include mountain regions where surface waters interact directly with glaciers, excluding most polar systems with limited terrestrial hydrology. Overall, this database provides the most comprehensive global synthesis of isotopic signatures from glacierized catchments. It supports applications such as: endmember mixing and hydrograph separation, calibration of isotope‑enabled hydrological models, assessment of moisture sources and continental climate gradients, reconstruction of past hydroclimatic processes using modern–paleoclimate linkages,  development of AI‑driven predictive models of cryosphere–hydrology interactions. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23184536

title: Machine Learning Accelerated Defect and Dopant Investigation in Inorganic Lead Halide Perovskites
description: This repository holds the relaxed structures and parsed doped data for HSE06 point-defect calculations in orthorhombic CsPbI3 and CsPbBr3. It covers native defects and extrinsic dopants (F, Cl, Br, I, O, S, Se, Te, N, P, As).  The top-level folder  has two subfolders, Structures and Doped_calc_jsons . Each of those is split into CsPbI3 and CsPbBr3 . Structures has one file per charged defect, plus Bulk.vasp for the pristine HSE supercell. Each file is the final relaxed CONTCAR of the HSE vasp_std run. It is renamed after its calculation directory, using doped naming: As_Cs_+1.vasp , v_Pb_-2.vasp , Br_i_Cs_Cs2.72_-1.vasp .  Doped_calc_jsons has the parsed doped data for each host. There are three kinds of files:   - Defect dictionaries: the native and extrinsic ones, saved as <host>_native_defect_dict_HSE.json and <host>_extrinsic_defect_dict_HSE.json .   - DefectThermodynamics files: the *_thermo_HSE.json files. Their names say what they cover:     - native defects     - one dopant ( extrinsic_As )     - grouped dopants ( P_As , O_S , Se_Te , F_Cl_Br or F_Cl_I )     - the equilibrium-concentration analysis ( eqm_* )     - the charge transition level diagrams ( CTL_* )   - HSE chemical potential files: cspbi3_hse_chempots.json for the native system, and cspbi3_hse_chempots_<El>.json for each dopant. CsPbBr3 follows the same pattern with   To evaluate the data, use the DefectThermodynamics class from doped.thermodynamics (https://github.com/SMTG-Bham/doped) .    The loaded object holds all the defect entries ( thermo.defect_entries ), the bulk VBM and the band gap ( thermo.vbm , thermo.band_gap ). From it the following can be obtained:   - formation energies at a given chempot limit and Fermi level, with get_formation_energies   - the charge transition levels, via thermo.transition_levels   - the equilibrium Fermi level and defect concentrations at a chosen temperature, with get_equilibrium_fermi_level and get_equilibrium_concentrations   - a formation energy diagram, with thermo.plot   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23427729

title: Materials and methods of an emerging shift in glacial erosion regimes on the Tibetan Plateau
description: Materials and Methods for “An Emerging Shift in Glacial Erosion Regimes on the Tibetan Plateau” This repository provides the numerical data and Python code supporting the analysis of glacial erosion dynamics and potential erosion-regime shifts in the Aksayqin and Ranwu lake basins on the Tibetan Plateau. The materials accompany a manuscript submitted to Geophysical Research Letters (GRL2). The study reconstructs glacial erosion rates over more than a century using lake sediment cores and examines their relationships with glacier dynamics, climatic conditions, and glacier retreat. The two basins represent contrasting glacierized environments, with higher glacier cover in Ranwu and lower glacier cover in Aksayqin. The repository includes three main computational components: Erosion–velocity scaling and parameter estimation. Nonlinear least-squares fitting and Bayesian inversion are used to constrain the power-law relationship between summer glacier velocity and reconstructed glacial erosion rates, expressed as ER = Kg × SGV^l. The analyses estimate the scaling coefficient (Kg), erosion exponent (l), and associated parameter uncertainties. Bayesian assessment of erosion regimes. Posterior distributions of the erosion exponent are examined to assess evidence for quarrying-dominated and potentially mixed quarrying–abrasion erosion. The threshold l = 1 is used to distinguish sublinear from superlinear erosion–velocity scaling. The Ranwu and Aksayqin basins are compared as a spatial analogue of different glacier-retreat states rather than as a directly observed temporal transition. Analysis of glacial erosion controls. Pearson correlation analyses quantify associations between reconstructed erosion rates and six climatic, glaciological, and sediment-connectivity-related variables: annual mean temperature, annual precipitation, glacier cover, lake area, glacier mass balance, and summer glacier velocity. These analyses support the comparison of erosion controls between the two basins. The accompanying Jupyter notebooks contain the computational procedures for model fitting, parameter uncertainty assessment, posterior visualization, correlation analysis, and figure generation. The Excel dataset provides the numerical variables used in these analyses. Together, these materials support the reproducibility of the quantitative analyses and provide a framework for investigating how glacier retreat may influence erosion–velocity scaling and reorganize glacial erosion controls under climate warming. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23355498

title: Metal-doping induced catalytic suitability of CoWO4@3D-printed electrode for nitrate reduction coupled glycerol oxidation
description: Multimetallic site engineering is emerging as a powerful strategy to regulate electronic structure and reaction pathways in complex multielectron electrocatalytic systems, such as electrocatalytic nitrate reduction. Here, we report the rational design of transition metal-doped CoWO 4 (M-CoWO 4 , M = Cu, Fe, Ni) integrated into 3D-printed octet lattice electrodes for the electrochemical conversion of nitrate to ammonia (NO 3 ⁻-to-NH 3 ) coupled glycerol oxidation (GOR). Systematic experiments, in situ Raman analysis and density functional theory calculations reveal that metal doping modulates the electronic environment around active sites through charge redistribution, thereby tuning intermediate adsorption and catalytic performance. Cu doping enhances NOₓ⁻ adsorption and lowers the energy barrier for sequential protonation steps, accounting for the superior ammonia production rate (∼2 mmol cm −2 h −1 ) and high Faradaic efficiency (95 %). By contrast, Fe doping preferentially enhances oxidative catalysis, including OER and GOR. In a full-cell configuration, GOR-coupled nitrate reduction decreases power consumption by ∼22 % and boosts NH 3 yield rate by 2.5-fold relative to the conventional NITRR||OER system. This study reveals that strategic metal doping in CoWO 4 tunes its electronic structure to promote energy-efficient NO 3 ⁻-to-NH 3 conversion coupled with glycerol oxidation, offering a sustainable pathway toward green ammonia production. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23492995

title: Metal-doping induced catalytic suitability of CoWO4@3D-printed electrode for nitrate reduction coupled glycerol oxidation
description: Multimetallic site engineering is emerging as a powerful strategy to regulate electronic structure and reaction pathways in complex multielectron electrocatalytic systems, such as electrocatalytic nitrate reduction. Here, we report the rational design of transition metal-doped CoWO 4 (M-CoWO 4 , M = Cu, Fe, Ni) integrated into 3D-printed octet lattice electrodes for the electrochemical conversion of nitrate to ammonia (NO 3 ⁻-to-NH 3 ) coupled glycerol oxidation (GOR). Systematic experiments, in situ Raman analysis and density functional theory calculations reveal that metal doping modulates the electronic environment around active sites through charge redistribution, thereby tuning intermediate adsorption and catalytic performance. Cu doping enhances NOₓ⁻ adsorption and lowers the energy barrier for sequential protonation steps, accounting for the superior ammonia production rate (∼2 mmol cm −2 h −1 ) and high Faradaic efficiency (95 %). By contrast, Fe doping preferentially enhances oxidative catalysis, including OER and GOR. In a full-cell configuration, GOR-coupled nitrate reduction decreases power consumption by ∼22 % and boosts NH 3 yield rate by 2.5-fold relative to the conventional NITRR||OER system. This study reveals that strategic metal doping in CoWO 4 tunes its electronic structure to promote energy-efficient NO 3 ⁻-to-NH 3 conversion coupled with glycerol oxidation, offering a sustainable pathway toward green ammonia production. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23532642

title: Modal Frequency Monitoring Data from the Marcus Aurelius Exedra Hall
description: This dataset contains modal frequencies identified from vibration measurements collected through long-term structural health monitoring of the Marcus Aurelius Exedra Hall at the Capitoline Museums in Rome, Italy. The dataset is provided as an Excel file containing time-stamped observations of three monitored modal frequency components: Date: date associated with each observation. f1 [Hz]: first monitored modal frequency, in hertz. f2 [Hz]: second monitored modal frequency, in hertz. f3 [Hz]: third monitored modal frequency, in hertz. The modal frequencies were identified from vibration measurements acquired at 3:00 p.m. using the covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification technique. The dataset contains only the modal frequency measurements; the corresponding temperature data were obtained separately from the Meteo Lazio™ amateur weather network ( https://www.meteoregionelazio.it ), using the Roma Colosseo weather station (latitude 41.885297, longitude 12.495091). The station is operated within the meteorological monitoring network associated with the Institute of Atmospheric Sciences and Climate of the National Research Council of Italy (ISAC-CNR) and is located a few hundred metres from the monitoring site, within a comparable urban and topographic setting. The temperature data were synchronized with the vibration measurements to establish the combined dataset used in the associated research. This combined dataset supports the investigation of temperature-induced variations in modal frequencies and the development and evaluation of probabilistic temperature-normalization methods for vibration-based structural health monitoring. The dataset is intended to support research transparency and reproducibility in the study of environmental effects on the dynamic response of lightweight steel–glass structures. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23469214

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation Data for AI-Designed Dual-Target Peptides Targeting APJ and DPEP1
description: Dataset Description This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled “An AI-driven rationally designed dual-target fusion peptide potently alleviates acute kidney injury.” The dataset contains molecular dynamics (MD) simulation data for 11 receptor–peptide complexes, comprising seven apelin receptor (APJ)–peptide systems and four dipeptidase-1 (DPEP1)–peptide systems. The receptor–peptide complexes were initially generated using Chai-1 structure prediction. All-atom MD simulations were conducted using GROMACS 2026.0 with the CHARMM36m force field and TIP3P water model. APJ complexes were embedded in explicit POPC lipid bilayers, whereas DPEP1 complexes were modeled in aqueous solution. Following energy minimization and equilibration, each system underwent a 200 ns production simulation. The archived dataset includes simulation topologies and associated parameter files, molecular structures, simulation input settings, production trajectories, available simulation logs, structural analysis outputs, and binding-energy calculation files. Analysis scripts for root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), peptide–receptor center-of-mass distances, hydrogen bonding, and binding-energy calculations are also provided. Binding-energy calculations were performed using gmx_MMPBSA, applying implicit-membrane MM/PBSA to APJ complexes and MM/GBSA to DPEP1 complexes. The data are organized by receptor and peptide system, with accompanying documentation to facilitate inspection and reproducibility of the computational analyses. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23611499

title: Monte Cimone 10-day LAGRANTO back-trajectories (2015-2025)
description: Product overview This dataset contains 11 years (2015-2025) of 10-day 3D air mass back-trajectories starting at Monte Cimone (44.19 °N, 10.70 °E, 2165 m a.s.l.), computed using the Lagrangian Analysis Tool LAGRANTO (Wernli and Davies, 1997; Sprenger and Wernli, 2015). The trajectories are calculated every 6 hours (at 00, 06, 12, and 18 UTC), by using the wind fields provided by the ERA5 reanalysis dataset of the ECMWF (Hersbach et al., 2020). Each file contains three back-trajectories, with starting points shifted by ± 50 hPa with respect to the station altitude. The temporal resolution of each back-trajectory is one point every hour. Files are provided in text format, with the filename as trajectory_yyyymmdd_hh , where hh is the UTC release time. Columns description time - time since the reference date (hours) lon - longitude, spanning −180 to 180 °E lat- latitude, spanning −90 to 90 °N p - pressure (hPa) TH - potential temperature (K) PV - potential vorticity (pvu) RH - relative humidity (%) Q - specific humidity (g/kg) PS - surface pressure (hPa) DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23590848

title: NATURAL-GEOGRAPHIC AND HYDROLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE SYR DARYA RIVER BASIN
description: The article provides a generalized natural-geographic and hydrological description of the Syr Darya river basin based on an analysis of classical and contemporary scientific literature. The position of the basin, the structure of its relief, its climatic conditions, the sources of river feeding and the features of the seasonal and long-term runoff regime are considered. Particular attention is paid to the division of the basin into a zone of runoff formation and a zone of runoff dissipation, which, in the author's view, is the key to understanding its water resources. It is shown that discrepancies in the published values of basin area and runoff are largely explained by differences in the boundaries and periods used by different authors. The results may serve as a basis for further hydrological modeling and water management planning. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23597706

title: NPP from brGDGTs
description: NOTE: 1. The R package to compute NPP from brGDGTs is available in https://github.com/MarcoVidalCordasco/envirolipids  2.  R_Code_and_Analysis_Guide.pdf facilitates navigation through the analytical workflow and helps identifying the code associated with each result presented in the study.  ## 📌 Overview This repository contains an R workflow for analysing branched GDGT (brGDGT) compounds and modelling **Net Primary Productivity (NPP)** using statistical and machine learning approaches. It also includes the full ecological modelling workflow to recosntruct herbivore biomass and carrying capacity of secondary consumers. There are two scripts: * Script_1 * Script_2 The Script_1 performs: * Exploratory data analysis * Statistical modelling (linear, quadratic, GAM) * Random Forest modelling with three validation strategies * Independent dataset validation * NPP reconstruction from Padul-15-05 core * Comparison with climate-derived NPP (Miami model) * Summed Probability Distribution (SPD) analysis for archaeological data * Correlation analysis * Summary statistics and plots The Script_2 performs: * Herbivore density estimations from primary productivity * Population structure modelling using survival curves * Biomass partitioning across body size classes * Secondary consumers carrying capacity calculations * Summary statistics and plots --- ## 📂 Data Requirements The Script_1 expects an Excel file: ``` Dataset_1.xlsx This contains: * A global dataset of present-day measured brGDGTs and associated climatic, edaphic and environmental variables * Areas with in-field NPP measurements * Climate conditions reconstructed in Padul * Archaeological sites, levels and dates for the summed probability distributions ``` The Script_2 expects two additional Excel files: ``` Dataset_2.xlsx This contains: * Herbivore traits (species, body mass, life history traits, etc.), * The wild mammal species list recovered in the region during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene (including sites and references) * NPP values (actual and potential) obtained from Script_1 * Primary and secondary consumer biomass summaries ``` ``` Prey_preferences.xlsx This contains: * Predator diet composition and annual biomass requirements ``` ## 📦 R Packages A package to apply the random-forest NPP predictions from brGDGTs is under construction --- ## ⚠️ Notes * Ensure working directory is set correctly: ```r setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path)) ``` * All files available in this repository should be saved into the same folder/directory --- ## 📬 Contact # mav54#cam.ac.uk DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23415332

title: Networked dataset for 'Socialecological affective arrangements: mapping with a small sea of many seas'
description: Network dataset for research paper 'Socialecological affective arrangements: mapping with a small sea of many seas' (under review). Contains a structured dataset of nodes and edges to be analysed with network algorithms. Original data was collected together with Dr. Paula Zuluaga-Guerra through eight qualitative interviews in the Mar Menor region (Murcia, Spain) in March 2022. The data was qualitatively analysed in October 2025, extracting the structured set of relations and nodes contained in this file. Relations (edges) refer to affects and emotions between socialecological entities and practices (nodes). The theoretical and methodological framework for this proposal is detailed in the paper together with an empirical illustration. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23594602

title: Numerical data supporting "Hidden Perturbative Structure in Attosecond Streaking"
description: This dataset accompanies the manuscript “Hidden Perturbative Structure in Attosecond Streaking” by J. Gao et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.24891 . The study demonstrates that symmetry filtering and Fourier analysis of the infrared fundamental in attosecond streaking reveal an effective two-photon s/d amplitude ratio that retains information about the continuum–continuum Fano propensity. SAE-TDSE numerical data The dataset contains original complex photoelectron amplitude matrices from single-active-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation (SAE-TDSE) calculations for helium at eight central XUV photon energies: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 atomic units . The matrices preserve the energy-, angular-momentum-, and pump–probe-delay-resolved amplitudes required to reconstruct photoelectron angular distributions and analyze their infrared-induced modulation. Each calculation includes 13 pump–probe delays. Numerical analysis and reproducibility The accompanying Python.tar archive contains four sequential Python processing scripts and the supporting matrix reader. The analysis proceeds through four stages: Reconstruction of the angle-resolved photoelectron intensity and isolation of its inversion-odd component. Extraction of the complex infrared-fundamental response by temporal harmonic analysis. Projection onto the odd Legendre coefficients A₁(E) and A₃(E). Evaluation of the energy-dependent effective complex amplitude ratio r_eff(E) = [6A₁(E)/A₃(E) − 4]/5, including its magnitude and phase. The extracted ratio is an effective observable derived from the angular and temporal response, rather than a direct measurement of individual microscopic two-photon transition amplitudes. The file PAHF_all8_edge_ratios_phases.csv summarizes representative emission- and absorption-edge values for the eight XUV energies. The file README.txt describes the matrix format, numerical parameters, Python dependencies, execution commands, intermediate outputs, and reference numerical values. Coulomb reference data The files L1abs and L1emi contain the original complex Coulomb continuum–continuum transition amplitudes for infrared absorption and emission, respectively. They provide the numerical reference for calculating the energy-dependent s/d amplitude ratios and relative phases. The accompanying Coulomb–SAE comparison figure displays these reference calculations as continuous curves and the extracted SAE-TDSE results as discrete points. Resonant UV streaking and circular RABBITT (Figure 3) The additional archive PAHF_Fig3.tar.gz provides the numerical inputs, Python scripts, and reconstructed PDF for Figure 3 of the manuscript, illustrating the energy dependence of the effective amplitude ratio and its phase in the near-threshold resonance region. The archive contains two independent numerical datasets: Linear streaking: Matrix90-400-11th.tar.gz contains 31 complex photoelectron amplitude matrices calculated at a central XUV photon energy of 0.9 a.u., with a 400-as XUV pulse and a 204-nm dressing field. The pump–probe delays span −120 to +120 a.u. in steps of 8 a.u. The archive retains the original input parameters and calculation log but excludes the momentum-distribution files not required for this analysis. Circular RABBITT: wEamo_Hel6m6N1_counterrot.zip contains five phase-resolved numerical datasets for counterrotating circular fields, with relative optical phases of −90°, −45°, 0°, +45°, and +90°. These provide the independent circular RABBITT comparison shown in Figure 3. The accompanying Python scripts reconstruct the complex effective ratio from the linear-streaking matrices and extract the circular RABBITT ratio through phase-harmonic and angular analysis. The two calculations produce the solid blue and dashed black curves, respectively, of Figure 3. The file Fig3_reconstructed.pdf provides the resulting two-panel comparison of the ratio

title: O'ZBEKISTONDA "YASHIL" ENERGETIKANI RIVOJLANTIRISH ISTIQBOLLARI

title: OZIQ-OVQAT XAVFSIZLIGI IQTISODIY MEXANIZMINING NARX MONITORINGI VA ZAXIRA BO'G'INI: HUDUDLARDA INTERVENTSIYANI ISHGA TUSHIRISH UCHUN OGOHLANTIRISH QOIDALARI
description: Annotatsiya. Maqolada hududlarda oziq-ovqat xavfsizligi iqtisodiy mexanizmining narx monitoringi va zaxira bo‘g‘ini - “qachon aralashish” savoli - uchta oddiy ogohlantirish qoidasi misolida retrospektiv sinovdan o‘tkaziladi. Qoidalar Qashqadaryo viloyatining 2025-yil yanvar - 2026-yil avgust oylik narx ma’lumotlarida tekshirildi: bir oylik o‘sish 1,0% dan kam emas (A qoida), uch oylik jamlama o‘sish 3,0% dan kam emas (B qoida), daromad o‘sishi bilan o‘n ikki oylik narx o‘sishi orasidagi farq 3 punktdan oshmaydi (C qoida). Respublika umumiy iste’mol narxlari indeksida A va B qoidalar bir martagina (2025-yil may) ishga tushgan. Uch oylik kuzatuv oynali qo‘shma qoida C ogohlantirishlarining 4 tasidan 2 tasini tasdiqlaydi. Chegaralar kalibrlanmagan, shu sababli natijalar ularning sezgirligini ko‘rsatadi. title: OpenET captures weaker daily evapotranspiration declines under combined atmospheric and soil-water stress: Data and code
description: This repository contains processed data, Python code, statistical results, figures, and documentation supporting an evaluation of daily OpenET evapotranspiration responses to combined atmospheric and soil-water stress. The study compares six OpenET models and their ensemble with eddy-covariance observations across the conterminous United States during 2016–2025. Processed paired datasets cover 202 sites, including 128 eligible for conditional stress analysis; SIMS is evaluated only at cropland sites. Materials include model-specific paired datasets, site metadata, climate covariates, crop-activity classifications, satellite imagery, flux-footprint contours, and scripts for statistical analyses and main and supplementary figures. The archive supports reanalysis from the supplied processed datasets and figure regeneration, with external source-data requirements and remaining upstream reconstruction steps documented in the README. Download all three ZIP archives and extract them into the same parent directory, merging the shared OpenET_Stress_Response_Release folder. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23324650

title: PDB-AI case study: atom-level electron-density loss in X-ray radiation-dose series (datasets and analysis package)
description: Datasets and analysis package for the case study in "Protein Data Bank Atomic Insights (PDB-AI): provenance-aware integration of structural biology resources" (Sellitto, Rolfe and Snell). The case study followed the same atoms through published X-ray radiation-dose series and found that the carboxylate oxygens of Asp and Glu lose electron density with dose faster than the amide oxygens of Asn and Gln in the same structures. The analysis was developed on 23 series (134 structures) and replicated under a pre-specified plan in 33 independent series. Every dataset was built with PDB-AI v1.0.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23572775) with every engine enabled. Files: pdbai_known_dose_atoms_public.csv.gz: PDB-AI output for the 134 structures of the 23 original series (682,311 atom rows; the columns empty in every row removed). original_134_build_records.zip: run summary with data dictionary, run manifest, entry list, and export, QC and coverage reports for that build. replication_pdbai_atom_site_dataset.csv.gz: PDB-AI output for the 351 structures of the replication series (1,090,479 atom rows). replication_atoms_analysis.csv.gz: the columns the replication analysis reads, without Asp/Glu residues refined at partial occupancy. replication_351_build_records.zip: run records, entry list and doses for that build. pdb-ai_case_study_v1.0.0.zip: the analysis package (a copy of PDB-AI v1.0.0, inputs, commands, environments, run records, scripts and outputs) that reproduces every result, figure and supplementary table of the case study. The published doses of the 23 original series are from Shelley and Garman (doi:10.5281/zenodo.5566557). The structural data derive from the PDB, PDB-REDO, wwPDB validation, UniProt and the AlphaFold Database, under their own terms. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23573387

title: POLARIZED ABSORPTION SPECTRA AND MAGNETIC ANISOTROPY OF THE Dy3+ ION IN DyAlO3: FROM J-MIXING TO MAGNETO-OPTICAL APPLICATIONS
description: Abstract.  Dysprosium orthoaluminate DyAlO 3  combines a strongly anisotropic Kramers ion with a low-symmetry (C s ) crystal-field site, which makes it a model system for relating optical selection rules to macroscopic magnetic anisotropy. This study analyses the polarized absorption spectra of the 6 H 15/2   → 6 F 3/2  band of Dy 3+  in DyAlO 3  at 77 and 300 K together with published magnetic and magneto-optical data. Eight Stark components recorded in two orthogonal polarizations in the ab plane were used to reconstruct the energies of the four lowest Kramers doublets of the ground multiplet (0, 53.7 ± 0.9, 125.7 ± 0.9 and 205.5 ± 0.3 cm −1 ) and the splitting of the excited 6 F 3/2  multiplet (10.1 ± 1.3 cm −1 ). Boltzmann analysis shows that 33% of the Dy 3+  ions occupy excited doublets at 77 K and 63% at 300 K, so the magnetic anisotropy observed above 100 K is controlled by the excited doublets rather than by the ground doublet alone. For a pure |±15/2⟩ ground doublet the model gives g ∥  = 20, g ⊥   ≈ 0 and a Curie constant along the Ising axis 2.6 times that of the free ion. Judd–Ofelt selection rules show that the 6 H 15/2   → 6 F 3/2  transition is governed by the Ω 6  parameter alone and that, in the axial approximation, only one of the two 6 F 3/2  sublevels can be reached from a pure |±15/2⟩ state. The observation of both components from the lowest doublet therefore requires J-mixing of the excited states. A two-site geometric model links the sign of the polarization anisotropy to the π or σ character of each transition. Single-oscillator analysis of the Faraday effect (λ 0  = 190 nm, 6.53 eV) indicates that the paramagnetic Verdet constant decreases 3.3-fold between 440 and 750 nm. The results support the use of DyAlO 3 in magneto-optical devices and low-temperature magnetic refrigeration. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23245342

title: PcfL MD and Phylogeny Files
description: This directory contains files related to the MD analysis and phylogenetic analysis contained in "Structural and mechanistic basis of N. aromaticivorans phenylcoumaran formaldehyde lyase catalysis via a quinone methide intermediate." The directory is split into GROMACS, Rosetta_Ligand_Docking, and Phylogeny subdirectories. Within the GROMACS subdirectory, a README file provides additional information about the MD analysis. Trajectories have been split out from the GROMACS directory into subdirectories grouped by ligand in the top level of the Zenodo due to their size large limiting our ability to upload them together. Where to find files mentioned in the manuscript: Tables of distance and occupancy calculations of key interactions for all trajectories (both all frames and bound frames) can be found in GROMACS/Calculations/FullCalculationsTables.xlsx. A spreadsheet containing additional information about the phylogenetic tree protein clusters can be found in Phylogeny/PhylogenyClustersRepresentativeProteins.xlsx. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23171909

title: Postprocessed Observational Records for Pakistan Rainfall Case
description: This store has been created to support the WCRP EPESC CEAA project. It contains Python scripts and a reference data file for the 2022 Pakistan Rainfall case study. It includes reference timeseries and climatologies for the two event definitions (seasonal and daily extremes) based on three observational products: ERA5, CPC, and MSWEP. Contents **regional_precipitation_indices_1979_2022.nc** is the reference data store. It contains processed timeseries from the three products. **calculate_regional_precipitation_indices.py** calculates two annual regional indices for each dataset: **Rx5d:** the annual maximum of rolling five-day accumulated precipitation (mm). **JA mean:** mean daily precipitation during July and August (mm/day).   It also calculates absolute and percentage anomalies relative to the 1991–2020 average, and writes the results to results/regional_precipitation_indices_1979_2022.nc. **plot_regional_precipitation_timeseries.py** reads that results file and creates a four-panel figure showing both indices and their percentage anomalies from 1979–2022, with 2022 values highlighted. Its output is figures/regional_precipitation_timeseries.png. **plot_2022_spatial_pr.py** reads the 2022 daily inputs and creates six maps: July–August mean precipitation and the 22–26 August accumulated total for each dataset. The maps mark Pakistan and the study region. Its output is figures/precipitation_spatial_distribution_2022.png. title: QPatLib v1.0 — Measurement-based quantum simulation Pauli string unitary pattern collections
description: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23620417

title: QUYOSH FOTOELEKTR ENERGIYASIDA ISHLAYDIGAN AVTONOM ATMOSFERA SUV GENERATORINING ENERGIYA SAMARADORLIGI: FARG'ONA VODIYSI UCHUN PSIXROMETRIK MODEL, TAJRIBAVIY KALIBRLASH VA ISH REJIMINI OPTIMALLASHTIRISH
description: Bug’ kompressorli atmosfera suv generatorlarining (AHSQ) solishtirma energiya sarfi (SES) yuqori bo’lib, quyosh fotoelektr stansiyasi (FES) bilan avtonom ishlaganda unumdorlikni bevosita cheklaydi; xorijiy qurilmalarning pasport ko’rsatkichlari (30 °C, 80 %) Farg’ona iqlimiga mos kelmaydi. Maqsad — ASG 02 (BWT-2) avtonom qurilmasi uchun eng kam energiya talab qiladigan ish rejimlarini nazariy va tajribaviy asoslash. Metodologiya. Farg’ona meteostansiyasining (WMO 38618) 1991–2020-yillar iqlim me’yorlari asosida kondensat (+5 °C) va muz (−3 °C) rejimlari uchun psixrometrik model tuzildi; model Trotec TTK 140S qurilmasining 24 nuqtali o’lchov ma’lumotlari bilan kalibrlandi va natijalar CPC–absorbsion hamda PV–kompressorli tizimlar bilan qiyoslandi. Natijalar. Aprel–oktabrda kondensat rejimi SESi 0,61–0,88 kVt·soat/l (ideal chegara), kalibrlangan real qiymat 1,52–2,52 kVt·soat/l; noyabr–martda suv faqat muz rejimida 1,09–1,56 kVt·soat/l sarf bilan olinadi. Kalibrlash tenglamasi SESreal = 3,70·SESmodel − 0,73 (R² = 0,937; MAPE 10,8 %). Tungi rejim SESni 32–60 %, kondensator issiqligi bilan muz eritish 12–20 % kamaytiradi. PV–kompressorli sxema 1 m² quyosh yuzasidan yiliga ~254 l suv beradi — CPC–absorbsion tizimdan (Tehron, 172 l) 1,5 marta ko’p. Ilmiy yangilik — Farg’ona uchun oylik rejim xaritasi, model–tajriba tuzatish koeffitsiyenti va birinchi qonun asosidagi SESmin mezoni. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23274088

title: Replication package for "War as an Asymmetric Shock for the EU Differentiated Integration System: Evidence from the Black Sea Basin" (Jakub Anusik & Rafał Riedel)
description: This archive contains the full data and R code to reproduce all results, tables and figures in the paper. The study uses a difference-in-differences design to estimate the effect of Russia’s February 2022 invasion of Ukraine on EU-integration progress across nine Black Sea economies (2014–2024), measured by a purpose-built Integration Progress Index (IPI) that aggregates treaty depth and institutional milestones. The package includes eleven numbered R scripts (data collection, index construction, the main DiD analysis, robustness and extended specifications, small-sample inference via CR2 and randomization inference, and figure generation), a master script ( 00_run_all.R ), the hand-coded source data and the pre-computed cleaned panel ( data/clean/ ), so the analysis can be reproduced offline. Full instructions, software requirements and a script-by-script guide are in README.txt . Requires R (≥ 4.2). The dependent variable (IPI) is hand-coded within the scripts; macroeconomic and institutional controls draw on the World Bank WDI and the V-Dem dataset. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23269792

The computational workflow used AutoDock Vina v1.2.7 with a 26 × 26 × 26 Å search box centred at 21.384, −17.788, 10.867 Å, exhaustiveness 32, up to 20 requested poses, and an energy range of 4 kcal mol−1. Native staurosporine redocking served as the structural-validation anchor. The archive includes receptor-preparation and structural-quality-control files, staurosporine redocking and RMSD calculations, the 12 ligand PDBQT inputs, production docking logs and poses, Mode-1 complexes, residue-contact analyses, candidate hydrogen-bond analyses, a file manifest and SHA-256 checksums. title: Reproducibility package for "Protonation States and Sampling Variability in Dupilumab–Excipient Molecular Dynamics" (version v33)
description: Analysis products, scripts and audit records underlying the manuscript "Protonation States and Sampling Variability in Dupilumab–Excipient Molecular Dynamics". Contents - allruns/ : per-condition analysis summaries and per-frame series for the 31   production runs of a dupilumab Fab–glucosamine–taurocholate assembly. - data/ : derived tables, including the 31-condition observable set, the   correlation-time table, the contrast screening table, the exact permutation   enumerations over all 27,720 group assignments, and the composition audit. - scripts/ : the analysis and figure scripts, with run_all.py reproducing the   derived tables and figures from the stored summaries in a fixed order. - series/, logs/, structures/, reference/ : retained per-frame series,   production logs, retained coordinates and reference tables. - MANIFEST.md lists every file with its SHA-256 checksum; BUILD_ORDER.md gives   the script execution order. - systems_H15_H60.tar.gz : the serialised OpenMM system definitions of the two   conditions whose systems were retained, H15 acidic and H60 intermediate,   with their SHA-256 checksums. - SYSTEMS_README.md : what those definitions record, including the OpenMM   version and the nonbonded settings they carry, and a charge-sum check that   can be repeated from them alone. Scope and limits Production trajectories were not retained. This package therefore reproduces the figures and tables from stored summaries; it is not an independent reanalysis of the atomic trajectories. Atomic geometry cannot be re-measured under a different contact cutoff, contact events cannot be re-extracted with censoring handled explicitly, and the residue tables cannot be extended beyond the stored entries. Serialized OpenMM system definitions and retained coordinates are available for two of the 31 runs only, the system definitions being supplied here as systems_H15_H60.tar.gz; the remaining runs have no equivalent verified system fingerprint. The package does not contain the instrument records behind the experimental section: the chromatograms, calibration series, unfolding curves and size-exclusion traces are not included, and the values in the Supporting Information tables are preparation-level summaries of those records rather than the records themselves. title: Role of Coupling Symmetry in Shaping the Electronic Coherence and Ultrafast Photoisomerization Dynamics of a Retinal Mode
description: This dataset contains the Hamiltonian parameters for four diabatic coupling models developed to investigate the ultrafast photoisomerization dynamics of  cis -penta-2,4-dieniminium ( cis -PSB3), a minimal model of the retinal chromophore. The three-dimensional Hamiltonian includes two diabatic electronic states, covalent (Cov) and charge-transfer (CT), and three nuclear coordinates: bond-length alternation (BLA), torsion (Tors), and hydrogen-out-of-plane wagging (HOOP). All four models share identical diabatic potential energy surfaces but differ in the functional form of the interstate coupling. The four coupling functions have similar absolute magnitudes but differ in reflection parity, sign pattern, and behavior near the planar cis / trans geometries and the intersection seam. These differences allow the investigation of how coupling symmetry affects electronic coherence, population transfer, and photoisomerization dynamics, even when the resulting adiabatic potential energy surfaces are nearly indistinguishable. The deposited Hamiltonian parameters correspond to the four coupling models employed in the quantum dynamics simulations reported in the manuscript Role of Coupling Symmetry in Shaping the Electronic Coherence and Ultrafast Photoisomerization Dynamics of a Retinal Model . The dataset is provided to facilitate the reproduction of the simulations and further investigations of coupling-dependent nonadiabatic dynamics. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23581074

title: SOCOMv2: Experiment 2 (GOBM subsampling experiment) full experimental dataset
description: Dataset Information Current Version: v2 (changelog at end of repository Contacts: Daniel J. Ford (d.ford@exeter.ac.uk) and Alizée Roobaert (alizee.roobaert@vliz.be)   The Surface Ocean CO2 Mapping program entered its second phase (SOCOMv2) with a range of experiments which provides a coordinated, community-driven framework to evaluate surface ocean fugacity of CO2 in seawater (sfCO2) reconstructions and derived air–sea CO2 fluxes under present-day observational constraints. This repository holds the dataset used within a Global Ocean Biogeochemical Model (GOBM) subsampling experiment designated Experiment 2, where nine fugacity of CO2 (fCO2) reconstruction methodologies reconstructed five GOBMs from the Global Carbon Budget 2023 (and one from 2024). The analysis and results of the study are presented in Roobaert et al. (in prep).  How to reference? If you use these data for a new analysis or publication, we request that you contact Alizée Roobaert (alizee.roobaert@vliz.be) and Daniel J. Ford (d.ford@exeter.ac.uk). This will allow the authors, and the SOCOM community the opportunity to contribute and be considered for co-authorship, depending on their level of involvement. If these data are used please reference the orginial study (Roobaert et al. 2026) and the repository with the version. Data format This dataset includes five individual zip files which contain a single netCDF file. Within each netCDF, the model fCO2sw and air-sea CO2 fluxes alongside the sfCO2 reconstructions and resulting air-sea CO2 fluxes. Ancillary information including for example model sea surface tmeperature and salinity, gas transfer, wind speed and a consistent mask where all data products provide an fCO2 estimate, are included within each file to aid interpretation of the data. Each zip file contains a netCDF file with the corresponding naming: SOCOMv2_Ex2_<model_name>_full_variables_<version>.nc where <model_name> is the model name from the five models, and <version> represents the dataset version. Model naming is shown in the table below: Model Name CESM_ETHZ_r1 FESOM2_REcoM IPSL_r1 MRI_ESM2_2 NorESM_vGCB2024 We refer the user to the netCDF file for the full set of avaiable variables but as a quick start: Model fCO2 are found under: model_sfco2 Model air-sea CO2 fluxes are found under: model_flux The corresponding data product fCO2 and air-sea CO2 fluxes are found by replacing 'model' with the corresponding dataproduct name. For example: VLIZ-SOMFFN_sfco2 Avaiable data products are: Dataproduct Name CarboScope-v2 CMEMS-LSCE-FFNN CSIR-ML6 JMA-MLR NIES-ML3 OceanSODA-ETHZv2 pCO2Residual UExP-FNN-U-v2 VLIZ-SOMFFN Changelog Version Changes since previous version v2 Updated CarboScope to a new version (now named CarboScope-v2 ) v1 Initial release of the dataset ready for submission of the supporting manuscript.   Acknowledgements AR, DJF, JDS, PL, GAM, TH, ARF, MG, JH and MGS were supported by the European Space Agency (ESA) through the ‘Ocean Carbon for Climate’ project (OC4C; contract number: 3-18399/24/I-NB). description: Ushbu maqolada sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining zamonaviy energetika sohasidagi o‘rni, aqlli elektr tarmoqlarini tashkil etish va boshqarish imkoniyatlari yoritilgan. title: Sagalassos Survey Database
description: The Sagalassos Survey Database publishes archaeological survey data from the Sagalassos Research Project study region in Burdur, Türkiye as Linked Open Data. The dataset documents survey projects, methods, survey areas, archaeological sites, features and geographical locations of interest, and selected external links such as Wikidata references. It is structured with CIDOC CRM, CRMsci, CRMSurv, CRMarchaeo, GeoSPARQL, and Dublin Core terms to support interoperable access to archaeological observations, site locations, feature classifications, survey methods, and related cultural heritage information. Coordinates are masked with a deterministic donut method (200-400 m offset) to protect site locations. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23505166

title: SegWeldCT: A Dataset of High-Resolution 3D Computed Tomography Scans of Welded Joints
description: Description SegWeldCT is a dataset of high-resolution industrial computed tomography (CT) scans of welded joints, developed to support research in automated weld inspection, internal defect analysis, and welding-process identification. It contains 30 reconstructed three-dimensional CT volumes of specimens produced using four welding processes: Metal Active Gas (MAG), Manual Metal Arc (MMA), Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG), and oxyacetylene welding. The specimens include both butt and fillet welds, providing variation in joint geometry, internal structure, and defect appearance. Dataset contents This release provides the original reconstructed 3D CT volumes in MetaImage (.mha) format. Each volume represents a complete scanned welded specimen and is about 2 GB. Volume dimensions vary between specimens. The data can be explored volumetrically or used to extract two-dimensional cross-sectional slices along the three principal axes. Data acquisition The welded specimens were scanned using a WidePIX A06-W0562-10 detector with technical support from RadalyX a.s. The reported acquisition settings were an energy threshold of 40 keV, an exposure time of 0.7 s, and a nominal voxel size of 0.055 mm (55 µm). We cleaned and aligned specimens before scanning under controlled conditions. No additional filtering or smoothing was applied to the reconstructed data, preserving the weld structure, defects, and acquisition-related image characteristics for subsequent analysis. Intended research applications The dataset supports research on: Volumetric characterization of welded joints and internal discontinuities. Automated weld-defect detection and localization. Welding-process classification from CT data. Development of 2D, 2.5D, and 3D learning approaches for industrial inspection. Computationally efficient processing of high-resolution CT volumes. The accompanying study investigates welding-process classification and binary defect segmentation using CT-derived slices. It describes a subset of 90 manually annotated 2D slices prepared with guidance from nondestructive-testing experts at the Institute of Criminalistics in Prague. This release does not include the derived slices and segmentation masks; it contains only the reconstructed 3D CT volumes. Data use and limitations The .mha volumes can be opened using software supporting the MetaImage format, including 3D Slicer. Users may extract cross-sectional images or prepare volumetric regions of interest to meet their research needs. For machine-learning evaluation, training, validation, and test partitions should be separated at the CT-volume level so that slices or patches derived from the same specimen do not appear in multiple subsets. The dataset contains a limited number of independent specimens, and the CT images may exhibit noise, blurring, and localized low contrast. Consider these characteristics when interpreting defect boundaries, designing annotation protocols, and assessing model generalization.     DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23591479

title: Short-Lived Post-Rainfall Surface-Moisture Windows and Projected Wind and Rainfall Extremes in Arabian Dune Landscapes
description: Processed data supporting Karimi et al., "Short-Lived Post-Rainfall Surface-Moisture Windows and Projected Wind and Rainfall Extremes in Arabian Dune Landscapes" (submitted to Catena), covering two dune landscapes in Saudi Arabia (Ar Riyadh and Mecca). MANIFEST.csv lists every file, the figure or table it supports, and its source. 00_study_area: regional boundary shapefiles and 250 m binary dune masks derived from a Sentinel-1 interferometric coherence mosaic (June–August 2021). 01_event_analysis: aligned daily ERA5 wind, GPM IMERG precipitation and ERA5-Land soil moisture (June 2000–December 2014), event thresholds, declustered event catalogues and event-dependence statistics. 02_wind: bias-adjusted NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 wind projections (SSP2-4.5, four GCMs): annual mean and p95 ensemble ranges, trends, GEV return levels, return-period shifts, annual maxima by model, and QDM calibration metrics. 03_precipitation: regional frequency-adapted QDM calibration metrics, distribution screening, and model-wise PE3 return levels for 3-day precipitation. 04_temperature: three-GCM annual mean temperature trajectories and inter-model ranges. 05_surface_state: dune-masked MODIS MOD13A2 NDVI and NDMI and ERA5-Land soil-moisture time series, with change-point, HAC trend and endpoint-sensitivity results. Source datasets: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (NASA), ERA5 and ERA5-Land (Copernicus Climate Change Service), GPM IMERG Final V07 (NASA), MOD13A2 V006/V061 (NASA). Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information (2026).
