title: Simulated XMM-Newton EPIC-pn spectrum with its ancillary response and redistribution matrix files
description: This record contains the three OGIP-format files needed to reproduce an X-ray spectral fit of a simulated XMM-Newton EPIC-pn spectrum: pn_pha.fits — type-I OGIP PHA spectrum (SPECTRUM extension, 4096 PI channels, exposure 100000 s, 190404 total counts). The spectrum is synthetic : it was generated with the XSPEC 12.13.1 fakeit command on 2026-02-10 from the model TBabs*vapec + TBabs(apec + apec + apec) folded through the response files listed below (keywords FKSRC001, FKRSP001, FKARF001, HISTORY). pn_arf.fits — ancillary response file (SPECRESP extension, 2067 energy bins, 0–15 keV), generated with arfgen 1.98.3 (SAS 17.0.0, xmmsas_20180620_1732) on 2020-05-23 using a flat detector map (detmaptype=flat, model effective area and quantum efficiency enabled). pn_rmf.fits — redistribution matrix file (MATRIX + EBOUNDS extensions, 2067 energy bins, 4096 channels), generated with rmfgen 2.6.1 (SAS 17.0.0, xmmsas_20180620_1732) on 2020-05-23 with a PSF-weighted detector map and threshold 1e-6. Instrument: XMM-Newton EPIC-pn (TELESCOP = XMM, INSTRUME = EPN), thin filter (FILTER = Thin1). The spectrum is not a real observation; no observation ID or pointing exists for it. The response files themselves are standard SAS products derived from the public EPIC-pn calibration. The three files are self-consistent: the RESPFILE and ANCRFILE keywords in pn_pha.fits point to pn_rmf.fits and pn_arf.fits respectively, so the spectrum can be fitted directly (e.g. with XSPEC) after loading the three files from this record. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23572188

title: Smile Synchrony as a Marker of Children's Group Interaction Quality
description: This project investigates smile synchrony in children's peer interactions during educational activities. Studying 187 children in 34 groups, we examine how directional smile synchrony emerges when children listen to a story and discuss it together. Using automatic smile detection and event-based analysis, we developed a novel method to quantify directional smile synchrony across all dyads within each group. Bayesian analysis revealed that groups with higher and more evenly distributed smile synchrony exhibited a more positive group climate, suggesting synchrony functions as a group-level marker of interaction quality. Key findings show that smile synchrony patterns differ by activity context: - During listening: synchrony correlated with gender similarity, national identity similarity, and perceived closeness to the emitter - During discussion: synchrony was heightened among extraverted children, those who felt closer to the group, and those who shared friendships This work demonstrates that smile synchrony captures meaningful variation in children's social engagement and reflects the interplay of interpersonal relationships, social identity, and personality. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18483832

title: Source data and plotting code for "Enhancing soil self-cleansing capacity for safe and productive agriculture"
description: Source data and plotting code for the figures of the article "Enhancing soil self-cleansing capacity for safe and productive agriculture". The article quantifies the self-cleansing of organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) in Chinese agricultural soils from 1980 to 2020, tests the effect of tillage intensity in five field experiments, and assesses an optimized reduced-tillage strategy and its costs and benefits. title: Storm Repair Permits from Municipal Records (Hurricane Harvey & Hurricane Ian)
description: Storm Repair Permits from Municipal Records: Hurricane Harvey (Houston, TX) and Hurricane Ian (Lee County, FL) — Version 2 This dataset contains all 961,960 municipal building permits filed in the 24 months after Hurricane Harvey (City of Houston, 649,314 permits) and Hurricane Ian (Cape Coral, Fort Myers, and Unincorporated Lee County, 312,646 permits), each scored by an LLM (Gemini 3.5 Flash) for whether it is a storm-caused repair. Every scored permit is included, not only high-scoring ones, so users can set their own thresholds and build their own labels. 163,835 permits score as likely storm repairs (p ≥ 0.90): 54,417 for Harvey and 109,418 for Ian. Permits are records, not buildings; a parcel can carry several permits. FILES - permits.parquet — one row per scored permit: raw LLM score (uncalibrated), LLM tier (STORM_REPAIR p ≥ 0.90; AMBIGUOUS; NOT_STORM_REPAIR p ≤ 0.30), pipeline identification layer, LLM peril (flood, wind/roof/tree, secondary repair, unrelated), work category, permit type and subtype, filing and final dates, declared valuation, privacy-redacted description, Census Block Group / tract / county FIPS, salted-hash project, parcel, and location keys, and, for Harvey, USGS/FEMA 3 m peak flood depths. - parcels.parquet — one row per hashed parcel: pre- and post-storm permit counts by tier, first storm-repair month, and a descriptive observation state. - annotations.parquet / annotations.csv — 504 permit entities each labelled independently by an internal and an external annotator (YES / NO / UNSURE and peril), pseudonymized, with sampling weights; linked to permits by project_uid. - DATA_CARD.md — full documentation: column definitions, records by layer and tier, human-validated storm-repair rates by tier and layer, Harvey inundation rates, privacy measures, and known limitations. - qa_report.json — results of 19 automated quality checks. - MANIFEST.json — input sources and checksums, row accounting, and output checksums. IMPORTANT CAVEATS - Labels describe permitted, storm-attributed repair, not damage. The absence of a storm-repair permit does not imply the absence of damage; permitting rates vary with income, insurance, tenure, and code enforcement. - Tiers are LLM outputs, not ground truth. In the human study, annotators agreed only modestly with each other (Cohen's kappa 0.22); see DATA_CARD.md for validated rates by tier and layer before using any tier as a label. - Storm-named permits (layer 1) are auto-accepted, not judged by the LLM. The non-candidate tier (layer 4) is the noisiest; filter or down-weight by identification_layer. - A declared valuation of 0 means no value was declared; treat it as missing. PRIVACY Owner, contractor, and applicant fields, street addresses, coordinates, and raw parcel and permit numbers are removed; identifiers are replaced by salted hashes and locations aggregated to Census Block Groups. Free-text descriptions are redacted in place: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, legal descriptions, and long identifiers are replaced by tags such as [NAME] and [ADDRESS], using each record's own identity fields, pattern rules, and Cloud Sensitive Data Protection. Redaction is not perfect, and exact filing dates and declared valuations are retained, so some records could be matched to the public municipal portals they originate from. CHANGES FROM VERSION 1 - All scored permits are included instead of p ≥ 0.90 only. - Descriptions are redacted; version 1 contained unredacted personal information in permit descriptions. - Exact duplicate records and permits filed outside the 24-month windows (which overlapped Tropical Storm Imelda and Hurricanes Helene and Milton) are removed. - Auto-accepted storm-named permits are flagged; missing values are no longer filled with defaults. - Parcel and human-annotation tables, a data card, a QA report, and a manifest are added. SOURCES AND LICENSE Raw permits are public records from the City

title: Structure, trajectory and force field data from all-atom MD simulations of different glycans used for B22 calculation
description: Collection of structure and trajectory files from long-box all-atom MD simulations of glucose, cellobiose, A2G2S2 and Man9 glycan pairs using different glycan force field - water model parameter sets for calculations of the osmotic second virial coefficient B22 via longbox simulations. Simulations are either classical MD (glucose, cellobiose) or enhanced sampled (A2G2S2, Man9). The force field parameter (.itp) files for the developed GLYCAM06-r60 force field, used in combination with the TIP4P-D water model, are included in the corresponding glycan-specific subfolders. Water and ions were removed from structures and trajectories to reduce file size. The subfolders of the repository are named according to the simulated glycan and used glycan force field - water model parameter set. Names follow the convention used in the associated publication.      DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.16880886

title: Supplementary Data 1 for What Rate Theories Compute: Triosephosphate-isomerase sensitivity calculation
description: Code and saved numerical results for the triosephosphate-isomerase sensitivity calculation in Section S6.4 and Figure S1 of What Rate Theories Compute: Chemical kinetics from Arrhenius to machine-learned potentials, by Rodney S. Ruoff (main text v9.12; Supplementary Materials v10.12).   The calculation independently implements the model, inputs, and conventions in code associated with the September 2022 version of I. Barr's bioRxiv preprint, DOI 10.1101/2021.08.04.454956. It compares two priors on six microscopic rate constants while retaining the same likelihood, other priors, and parameter bounds. The archive contains Python scripts, saved posterior samples, likelihood-profile fits, numerical summaries, diagnostics for lower rate ceilings, and the code and results for Figure S1. The README gives reproduction instructions and defines the energy and rate conventions.   The calculation does not reproduce the posterior reported in the July 2023 revision of Barr's preprint. No new experimental measurements are included. Barr's original code is not redistributed in this archive.  DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23557458

title: Supplementary Dataset and Clustering Logs: Unsupervised Motif Discovery in Engineering Processes
description: This repository contains the supplementary materials and experimental data supporting the research article: “Unsupervised Motif Discovery in Engineering Processes: A Machine Learning Approach Using Graph-Based Segment Embeddings”. The dataset is divided into four primary components: the corpus of 46 System Dynamics models, the clustering logs and contingency tables, the evaluated feature configurations, and a summary of the key empirical findings. 1. Model Corpus This section contains the 46 System Dynamics models used in the study. Each model is a directed graph whose nodes are Stocks, Valves, Variables or Clouds, connected by Flow and Influence links, and each node carries its mathematical formula. Each model also includes its simulation settings (time horizon and integration time step). All variable names, annotations and textual descriptions were removed before analysis, so the models contain only structural and mathematical information. File model_corpus.csv : A C# source file containing the 46 models as a list, one entry per model, each with its JSON definition and engineering domain: Bio-engineering (11 models), Chemical Processes (12 models), Energy Systems (11 models) and Environmental Systems (12 models). The domain labels serve as the ground truth for post-hoc evaluation only and were never presented to the clustering algorithm. The file can be included directly in a .NET 10.0 project. 2. Experimental Logs and Clustering Results This section contains the outputs of the K-Means clustering pipeline implemented with ML.NET v4.0.2 on .NET 10.0 (Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen PRO 7840U). Each configuration was run 4 times for every number of clusters K from 2 to 5, with fixed seeds given by seed = 42 + (K × 100) + (run × 7), run = 0–3. All runs are exactly reproducible. All CSV files are semicolon-delimited, UTF-8 encoded and use a decimal comma. File experiment_run_manifest.csv : Experiment settings, including the run profile, corpus size, selected K, K grid, runs per configuration, seed schedule, generation time (UTC) and evaluated configurations. File clustering_metrics_summary.csv : Mean and standard deviation over the 4 runs of the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI, arithmetic-mean normalization), Silhouette score and Davies-Bouldin index, for every configuration and every K from 2 to 5. ARI and NMI are computed on the 46 model-level labels obtained by plurality voting over each model’s segments. Silhouette and Davies-Bouldin are computed on the segment vectors, or on the 46 model vectors for the WholeModel baseline. Files ablation_results_whole-model.csv , ablation_results_bag-of-nodes.csv , ablation_results_topology-lite.csv and ablation_results_full.csv : Detailed results of the representative run (K = 4, seed 442) for each configuration. Each file has three sections separated by blank lines: run metadata, the cluster–domain distribution with counts and percentages, and the four clustering metrics. Files contingency_table_whole-model.csv , contingency_table_bag-of-nodes.csv , contingency_table_topology-lite.csv and contingency_table_full.csv : Cluster–domain contingency tables (model counts) of the representative run (K = 4, seed 442). Cluster indices are arbitrary and not comparable across configurations. 3. Evaluated Configurations (Ablation Study) The experiments compare one holistic and three segment-level representations. The segment-level representations parse each model into typed structural segments (Feedback Loops, Causal Paths and Stock-Flow Subsystems). The configurations are: WholeModel : A single feature vector per model (baseline), requiring no assignment step. Bag-of-Nodes : 8 constituent-composition features per segment (counts of Stocks, Valves, Variables, Clouds, Flows and Influences, and total numbers of nodes and links). title: Supplementary Materials from: Airborne Particulate Matter Removal by Filters Containing Graphene Oxide based Materials: A Systematic Review
description: This repository contains the bibliographic datasets, bibliometric analysis files, review protocol, and supplementary materials supporting the review: “ Airborne Particulate Matter Removal by Filters Containing Graphene Oxide-based Materials: A Systematic Review ”. The review follows the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework and examines the preparation, structural characteristics, filtration performance, and applications of filters containing graphene oxide and its derivatives. Searches covered English-language research articles published between 1 January 2000 and 1 September 2026 in Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection. A total of 392 records were retrieved, and 49 studies met the eligibility criteria. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Bibliometric analyses were conducted using VOSviewer version 1.6.21. The repository contains: Bibliographic database exports: scopus_raw_data.csv and web_of_science_raw_data.csv , containing records retrieved from the respective databases; Included-study records: reviewed_papers_scopus_format.csv , containing bibliographic records for the 49 studies included in the review, organized in Scopus format; Search results summary: search_results.csv ; Bibliometric analysis exports: files supporting analyses of authors, countries, keywords, and co-citations in VOSviewer; Thesaurus files: thesaurus_terms_countries.txt and thesaurus_terms_keywords.txt , used to harmonize country names and keyword variants; Review protocol and supplementary materials: Supplementary_R2.docx documentation of the review question, search strategy, eligibility criteria, study selection, data extraction, and synthesis procedures, together with supplementary bibliometric figures. The raw data files contain bibliographic records exported from the databases. These materials are shared to support verification, methodological transparency, and reuse in subsequent systematic reviews and bibliometric studies. This updated release corresponds to the revised review completed in October 2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23454474

title: Supplementary code, data and the computed equation of state for "The maximum neutron-star mass from a cumulant equation of state: coherence structure, a microscopic foundation to twice saturation, and the super-conformal core demanded by observation"
description: Supplementary code, input data and reference outputs accompanying “The maximum neutron-star mass from a cumulant equation of state: coherence structure, a microscopic foundation to twice saturation, and the super-conformal core demanded by observation” by Andrei Tudor Pătrașcu, New Astronomy, DOI 10.1016/j.newast.2026.102664. The deposit preserves the supplementary package associated with the September 2026 revised manuscript. It contains the microscopic cumulant calculations and controls, equation-of-state and stellar-structure pipeline, observational constraints with references, Bayesian high-density-extension results, and explicit finite-Fock-space checks for Appendix A. The ZIP includes execution instructions, Python source, input tables and saved reference outputs. The separately downloadable cumulant_eos_table.dat is identical to SI/data/cumulant_eos_table.dat in the archive. Its columns give baryon density, energy density, pressure, squared sound speed and proton fraction for the three-body normalisation F = 0.68, plus pressures at F = 0.56 and 0.85. The header gives units; the SLy4 crust table for densities below 0.03 fm^-3 is included in the archive. After unpacking, run bash run_all.sh from SI; dependencies and individual controls are documented in SI/README.md. The full Bayesian posterior grid is supplied as reference data; its separate regeneration command is documented in the README. Scope: the microscopic equation of state is benchmarked against quantum Monte Carlo up to twice nuclear saturation density. The higher-density extension is causal and constrained by observations; it is not claimed to be a first-principles high-density calculation. This deposit freezes the accepted-paper supplementary materials and does not introduce a new scientific revision. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23242461

title: Supplementary materials for the doctoral thesis "Soil Microbial Communities and Functional Potential along the Chilean Coastal Cordillera: Insights from DNA-Pool Separation and iDNA Metagenomics"
description: Supplementary materials for Chapters 2–4 (Appendices A–C) of Xiuling Wang’s doctoral thesis, “Soil Microbial Communities and Functional Potential along the Chilean Coastal Cordillera: Insights from DNA-Pool Separation and iDNA Metagenomics”. Version 1.0.5 updates the public supplements to the current thesis and the metagenomic manuscript submitted to Environmental Microbiome on 19 October 2026; submission does not imply acceptance. Appendix A / Chapter 2: Tables A1–A6 and Figures A1–A12. Appendix B / Chapter 3: Tables B1–B5, Figures B1–B6 and Protocol B1 for DNA-pool separation. These files retain their released numerical results and protocol procedures. Bacterial figures reproduce the published article supplement with thesis numbering. Appendix C / Chapter 4: Tables C1–C4, Figures C1–C3 and Data C1. The two workbooks are byte-identical to the 19 October 2026 submission; their internal journal S identifiers are retained and mapped explicitly in README.md. Data C1 now contains ten worksheets; its older filename is retained for link continuity, but its scope is broader than KO differential abundance. Figure C2 spans two pages. Figures C1–C3 use current thesis image variants, with higher-rank taxonomic names in roman type, and current submitted English captions. Compared with public version 1.0.4, this release adopts Appendix A–C filenames, updates the two metagenomic workbooks and supplementary figures, and adds an updated file guide and checksums. No thesis manuscript, unpublished isolate manuscript, correspondence or additional local-only source-data collection is included. Previous public releases and source manuscripts remain unchanged. title: Supporting Data for "Mapping Emerging Green Skill Domains for the Manufacturing Workforce A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis"
description: This dataset supports the study entitled “Mapping Emerging Green Skill Domains for the Manufacturing Workforce: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis.” It documents the research process used to examine the literature on green skills and sustainable manufacturing through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis. The dataset is intended to support research transparency, reproducibility, and further investigation into green skill requirements for manufacturing workforce development. The materials may include the search strategy and search strings, study screening records, data extraction from included studies, bibliometric analysis outputs, and thematic coding used to identify five overarching research themes and 11 candidate green skill domains. These domains cover technical, environmental management, circular economy, digital–green manufacturing, innovation, cognitive, behavioural, social, adaptive, strategic, and leadership capabilities. The dataset is intended for researchers, vocational education and training institutions, manufacturing practitioners, and policymakers interested in green skills, workforce development, and sustainable manufacturing. It can support further research, curriculum development, training-needs assessment, and the empirical validation of the proposed green skill taxonomy. Only files and data that are available and permissible to share are included in this record. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23397827

title: Swiss Dwellings: A large dataset of apartment models including aggregated geolocation-based simulation results covering viewshed, natural light, traffic noise, centrality and geometric analysis
description: Introduction This dataset contains detailed data on over 45,000 apartments (370,000 rooms) in ~3,100 buildings including their geometries, room typology as well as their visual, acoustical, topological, and daylight characteristics. Additionally, we have included location-specific characteristics for the buildings, including climatic data and points of interest within walking distance. Changelog v3.0.0 (2023-03-31): Updated the dataset increasing the total number of apartments to 45176 and incorporating fixes to some of the sites. The update includes re-digitized apartments and thus alters some ID values. v2.2.1 (2023-03-10): A file, location_ratings.csv , has been included to provide ratings of the locations in which the buildings are situated. The ratings, provided by  Fahrländer Partner AG , give insights into the living situation at the buildings' addresses. Details for the different dimensions are provided below. The file  location.csv  has been updated to include the minimum and maximum temperatures for the locations in which the buildings are situated. v2.1.0 (2022-12-23) : A file, locations.csv , has been included to provide information on the climatic and infrastructural characteristics of the locations in which each building is situated v2.0.0 (2022-10-17): Additional to the residential units, we also include the commercial and public parts (such as staircases) of the models. The field unit_usage  describes whether an area belongs to a commercial, residential, janitor or public part of the building Added the fields  elevation  and height  to  geometries.csv  to describe the elevation above the terrain surface and the height of objects. Added the field  plan_id  which allows identifying which floors are based on the same floor plan (in some cases multiple floors of a building share the same floor plan Improved the ordering of fields in the CSV files (instead of alphabetic order) Minor changes to individual sites Procurement The data is sourced from commercial clients of  Archilyse AG  specializing on the digitization and analysis of buildings. The existing building plans of clients are converted into a geo-referenced, semantically annotated representation and undergo a manual Q/A process to ensure the accuracy of the data and to ensure a maximum 5%-deviation in the apartments' areas (validated with a median deviation of 1.2%). title: THE ROLE AND PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF GEYSLER ALLOYS IN MODERN MATERIALS SCIENCE
description: Heusler alloys represent an important class of functional intermetallic materials with highly tunable structural, electronic, magnetic, mechanical, and thermoelectric properties. Their scientific significance is associated with the possibility of controlling physical characteristics through chemical composition, atomic ordering, valence-electron concentration, and structural phase transformations. Full-Heusler, half-Heusler, inverse-Heusler, and quaternary Heusler systems have attracted considerable attention because of their potential applications in spintronics, thermoelectric energy conversion, magnetic refrigeration, shape-memory technologies, sensors, actuators, and emerging quantum materials. This article examines the structural characteristics, functional properties, practical applications, and research perspectives of Heusler alloys. Particular attention is paid to their half-metallicity, spin polarization, martensitic transformations, magnetocaloric behavior, and thermoelectric performance. The role of computational materials science, density functional theory, and machine-learning-assisted materials design in developing new Heusler compounds is also discussed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23255921

title: THE USE OF ANGLICISMS IN GERMAN AND THEIR IMPACT ON THE LEXICAL SYSTEM
description: Abstract. The rapid spread of English as a global language has significantly influenced the vocabulary of contemporary German. This thesis examines the use of Anglicisms in German, the main domains in which they occur, the mechanisms of their phonological, morphological, orthographic and semantic adaptation, and their impact on the German lexical system. The study is based on descriptive and comparative analysis of commonly used examples such as Computer, Smartphone, Meeting, Feedback, downloaden, posten and liken. The findings show that Anglicisms perform several functions: they nominate new realities, increase lexical economy, create stylistic effects and contribute to word-formation productivity. At the same time, excessive or unnecessary borrowing may cause competition with native equivalents and raise questions of comprehensibility and language policy. Overall, English borrowings should be regarded not simply as foreign elements, but as an important mechanism of lexical development in present-day German. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23220594

title: TRENDS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CASHLESS SETTLEMENTS AND REMOTE BANKING SERVICES IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
description: Abstract. This article examines the development trends of cashless settlements and remote banking services in commercial banks of Uzbekistan from the perspective of enhancing the accessibility and widespread use of banking services. Based on regulatory and legal documents, reports of the Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and empirical data on commercial banks operating in Andijan Region, the study analyzes the current state of electronic payment infrastructure, the use of bank cards and alternative digital payment instruments at fuel filling stations, as well as disparities across regions and banks. The study substantiates the necessity of assessing the development of cashless settlements not merely by the number of payment instruments available, but also by their actual utilization rate, transaction volumes, the share of active cards, territorial coverage, and customer activity. The mechanism through which the widespread adoption of remote banking services affects banks’ financial stability via the expansion of the customer base, growth in banking turnover, commission income, and strengthening of the resource base is also examined. Based on the findings, scientific and practical recommendations aimed at improving the efficiency of digital payment services are proposed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23220266

Sampling encompassed teredinid-bored large woody debris (LWD), Rhizophora prop roots and mangrove sediments. Additional measurements characterise vacant teredinid tunnel area and its associations with macrofaunal richness, abundance and occupancy. The deposit includes supporting datasets, statistical outputs and methodological documentation. These materials support examination and reuse of the ecological patterns reported in the accompanying manuscript.   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23435374

title: Trends in occupancy of Odonata species in north-west Italy
description: This dataset contains the underlying data for the article "Trends in occupancy of Odonata species in north-west Italy - marked changes over two decades (2005–2025)" by Gianandrea La Porta & Sönke Hardersen Aim: This study aims to characterise long-term occupancy dynamics of Odonata assemblages by estimating occupancy trends for each species individually, for species grouped according to three ecological traits (thermal tolerance, habitat preference, and habitat specialisation), and for overall diversity using a multi-species occupancy model. Location: The study area comprised the continental biogeographic region of Piedmont and Lombardy (north-west Italy), covering 59,000 km², with much of the area belonging to the Po Valley. Methods: Species occupancy was estimated from 87,464 georeferenced occurrence records collected with two citizen science platforms. Bayesian dynamic occupancy models were applied at three levels: single-species, trait-groups, and community level. Results: 16 out of the 53 species analysed showed a significant increase and 28 a significant decline in occupancy between 2005 and 2025. The most pronounced losses were recorded among cold-adapted and lentic/temporary-water species. Community-level occupancy fell from 43.8% to 36.0% over the same period. Main Conclusions: These findings indicate that multiple factors, including climate change and habitat modification, are reshaping the odonate community, favouring warm-adapted generalists over cold-adapted specialists. Moreover, the overall decline in occupancy reported here should be regarded as a lower-bound estimate of the actual loss of odonate abundance in the study area. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23588094

title: Two-Stage Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis Framework for Comparative Customer Preference Analysis of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles
description: Dataset Description This dataset supports the research study entitled “Two-Stage Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis Framework for Comparative Customer Preference Analysis of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles.” The dataset was developed to investigate consumer preference toward battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) through Indonesian-language YouTube automotive discussions. It contains user-generated comments collected from eight Indonesian automotive videos covering electric vehicles, hybrid vehicles, and comparative vehicle discussions. The research corpus initially contained 10,079 comments collected between June 12, 2022, and September 28, 2026. Following data cleaning and preparation, 9,948 comments were retained for analysis. The preparation process addressed duplicate records, empty comments, automated or repetitive comments, and textual noise while preserving relevant automotive terminology and negation. The research applies a two-stage analytical framework. Stage 1 classifies comments into EV Preference, Hybrid Preference, and Neutral/Non-preference categories. A manually annotated dataset was created through independent annotation by three annotators, with consensus labels used for model development and evaluation. Stage 2 examines aspect-level sentiment across four categories informed by the Value-based Adoption Model (VAM): Price and Resale Value, Energy Efficiency and Operating Cost, Performance and Reliability, and Infrastructure and Technology Features. The dataset is intended to support research in Indonesian natural language processing, consumer preference analysis, sentiment analysis, aspect-based sentiment analysis, and electric and hybrid vehicle adoption. Where applicable, the shared files include anonymized comment identifiers and analytical labels. Personal identifiers should not be included in the public release. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23439876

title: UAV-LiDAR, field inventory and coastline data for two Avicennia germinans chronosequences, Coronie, Suriname (2024)
description: Field, wood, soil, UAV laser scanning (ULS) and coastline data, with the analysis code, from two coast-perpendicular Avicennia germinans chronosequences on the mudbank coast of Coronie, Suriname. The data underlie: Feyen J. et al. Structural development of Avicennia mangrove forests along a successional chronosequence on the Suriname coast revealed by UAV laser scanning and field inventory  (in preparation). Study design 35 circular plots (12.5 m radius) were laid out at 100 m intervals from the seaward mangrove edge along two transects: T1 near Perseverance (20 plots, crossing a chenier ridge) and T2 near Jenny (15 plots). Stand ages range from 5 to ≥ 36 years, derived from annual Landsat classifications (1988–2024). Fieldwork and UAV flights took place in September 2024. Contents Coronie2024_code.zip data/ Plot data ( Coronie2024_field_plot_data.csv ): stand age, seaward distance, chenier position, stem density, basal area, diameters, heights, species composition, aboveground biomass with Monte Carlo uncertainty (Chave et al. 2014; BIOMASS), basic wood density and wood anatomy from increment cores, soil organic carbon to 30 cm and 1 m, soil EC and pH per depth, and porewater salinity. Tree data ( Coronie2024_tree_data.csv ): 1321 stems with species, DBH, measured and modelled height, decay class and assigned wood density. ULS metrics ( Coronie2024_ULS_MC_iterations.csv , Coronie2024_ULS_plot_data.csv ): over 100 structural metrics (height, vertical heterogeneity and complexity, plant area, canopy cover, gaps, canopy volume) for 100 Monte Carlo realisations of each plot centre, which propagate the ~5 m GPS uncertainty, plus plot medians and SDs. Shorelines ( Coronie2024_shorelines.gpkg ): the annual seaward mangrove edge, 1988–2025, from Landsat imagery. Spatial layers ( Coronie2024_spatial.gpkg , Coronie2024_plot_centres.csv ): centres of all 35 plots, 50 m clip footprints, and a tile index showing which point-cloud tile covers each plot. README.md (methods, conventions, instructions), CITATION.cff , licences. Coronie2024_transect_T1.zip , Coronie2024_transect_T2.zip Point clouds : height-normalised point clouds of both full transects, homogenised to 750 pulses m⁻²; the ULS metrics were computed from plots clipped from these clouds. Acquired with a DJI Matrice 300 RTK carrying a DJI Zenmuse L2 (47 m altitude, 240 kHz, ~3300 points m⁻² before thinning), RTK-corrected. Licences and funding Data and point clouds: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT. Funded by the Global Climate Change Alliance (GCCA+ 2) project “Strengthening the Mangrove Forest Monitoring System” (SUR/2021-019) and the PRSUMF project (SUR-2025-034). Field and logistical support: Foundation for Forest Management and Production Control (SBB) and the Centre for Agricultural Research in Suriname (CELOS). DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23343843

title: ULE Framework Scoring Dataset: Istanbul and New York City
description: Version 4 — aligned with the other scoring records in this series; references to unpublished text removed; scoring report regenerated; no score changed This version changes no score symbol and no numeric value. Istanbul and New York City keep the profiles deposited in version 1. It corrects five cells and five inventory rows on a cross-check against the later records in this series that score the same jurisdictions, replaces a scoring report that had not been regenerated since version 1, and removes from this description two references to text that is not published. Cells corrected, scores unchanged New York City E5 (epistemic translation). Versions 1 to 3 rested this cell on the annual Stormwater Management Program revision cycle described in the 2025 MS4 Annual Report. description: Version 5 — one score corrected, and the record brought onto the current schema This version does three things: it corrects one score, it migrates the record from the nine-field schema used since version 1 to the twenty-two-field specification of the codebook, and it removes a superseded vocabulary. No evidence is discarded and nine of the ten scores are unchanged. The corrected score Türkiye, financial endowment (E3), moves from absent to partial. The earlier value rested on two findings that remain true: no dedicated municipal budget line was identified in the 2023 metropolitan budget documentation, and research-council grants fund projects rather than governance platforms. What has changed is the law. Act 7552 of 2025, which postdates the original coding, hypothecates emission permit charges, primary-market allowance sales, half of the market operator's trading-system revenues and half of the administrative fines to a revolving fund held by a central body, under Article 12. That is a standing mechanism rather than one contingent on a particular project, which takes the condition off absent. It is attached to no instrument and to no territory, which keeps it below substantial. The Türkiye total moves from 2 of 10 to 3 of 10. This is a revision on new law rather than a correction of a misreading, and the record says so. The same value is recorded in the United States and Türkiye scoring record (10.5281/zenodo.23280735), and the two records now agree on every Türkiye cell. The schema migration Versions 1 to 4 carried nine fields: condition_code, condition_name, country, score_symbol, score_numeric, operational_definition, evidence_summary, primary_source and failure_mode_implication. The codebook specification now requires twenty-two. The migration carries evidence_summary, primary_source and failure_mode_implication into provision_relied_upon, coding_reasoning and source_document, and adds the fields the specification requires: level_scored, provision_form, provision_bindingness, legal_condition_tier, levels_searched, contested, candidate_scores, contested_reason, reread_status, e5_component_absent, durability_class, score_in_prior_record and revision_note. Three of the added fields are derived rather than freshly coded. The tier of legal condition, the class of legal force and the durability class were derived from the provisions already recorded in each row, under codebook rules 6.9, 6.8 and 6.10, and each row says so in its revision note. They are marked for confirmation by the coder rather than presented as independent readings. The staged double reading of rule 6.6 is not claimed for the nine cells carried unchanged. The rule in its present form postdates the original coding of this record, and a record that marks a cell as double read when no second reading was performed misstates its own procedure. Each cell records that explicitly rather than leaving the field empty. The superseded vocabulary Versions 1 to 4 described funding using a three-part typology, K1, K2 and K3, which has no counterpart in the codebook and belongs to an earlier formulation of the framework. It is removed. The codebook records the same distinction under rule 6.10, as the class of legal form from which an obligation arises: L1 a court order, consent order or permit condition; L2 a standing institutional agreement or statutory formula; L3 an appropriation; L4 a competitive award. Where the earlier record said "K1 base", the present record says that the obligation arises from a statutory formula and records L2. The substance is preserved; the vocabulary is now the one the codebook defines. The numeric value, 2, is unchanged. Two Turkish instruments are named by their statutory titles. The 2014 regulation is Mekânsal Planlar Yapım Y&o

description: Version 7 — Netherlands legal bases re-read against the consolidated statutes; one score changed; Turkish initiative inventory added This dataset records the Urban Living Lab Legal Enablement (ULE) scoring of the Netherlands and Türkiye on the five enablement conditions E1–E5, together with the documentary inventory from which every score is derived. Scoring follows the ULE codebook and scoring protocol, deposited separately and fixed before either case was scored: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21645631. The version governing this scoring is codebook 3.2. Codebook 3.3, published after this scoring was completed, adds a figure, brings the field templates into line with its own Section 9 and corrects editorial matter; it changes no decision rule and no score in this record. Files in this version ule_scores_nl_turkiye.csv — Ten scored cells, one row per condition and jurisdiction, in the twenty-two-field schema of codebook Section 9. document_inventory_nl_turkiye.csv — The instruments and documents examined, with legal force class, persistent identifier, access date, inclusion rationale and the conditions each informs. turkish_initiatives_inventory.csv — The five Turkish initiatives observed in interview-based fieldwork, in the initiative-inventory fields of codebook Section 9: thematic focus, period active, initiating actor, organisational housing, legal personality, coordination model, ecological orientation, funding arrangement and the inclusion criterion recording why each was counted. Fields are taken from the published account of the fieldwork (Çelik Yılmaz and Ertekin 2026, Cities 169, 106514). The United States and Türkiye scoring record carries the same five initiatives from the same source; where the two files record the same fact — funding, planning authority, ecological orientation, the ground of inclusion — they agree, and descriptive fields are worded independently. A field the source does not establish is recorded as "not established" with the reason. No score depends on this file: an initiative inventory documents activity and nothing more. Initiatives operating where a condition is absent establish that the absence did not prevent activity from arising, not that the absence is the constraint on anything else. Whether a recorded deficit binds, and on what, requires evidence about the deficit. How to read the output The output of this scoring exercise is an ordered profile and a break position — the first condition falling below full institutional presence — not a scalar total. A total collapses structurally different profiles to one value and lets strength on one condition stand in for a deficit on another; these conditions do not compensate for each other. The profiles recorded here are:   E1 E2 E3 E4 E5 Break Netherlands partial partial partial partial partial E1 Türkiye absent partial partial partial absent E1   Both break at the first condition and no condition in either jurisdiction reaches full institutional presence. The profiles differ in depth rather than in break position. How to read an absent score A score of absent records that no provision satisfying the condition is identified in the corpus listed in document_inventory_nl_turkiye.csv, as the instruments stood at the cut-off date. It is a statement about the corpus, not about the legal system. Where a cell rests on absence, the instruments searched are named in the cell, so the finding can be tested by adding an instrument rather than by argument. description: Version 4 — a corrected score, and why it was wrong This version corrects one score. Portland, governance empowerment (E2), moves from substantial to partial. The other fourteen scores are unchanged, as is the corpus. What version 3 recorded. The cell was scored substantial on the statutory watershed management authority of Portland's Bureau of Environmental Services within the Urban Services Boundary, combined with formally recognised watershed councils in Johnson Creek, Fanno Creek and Columbia Slough, and a regional tier in Metro. The reasoning held that authority was assigned to named actors with defined accountability at both agency and community levels. Why that was wrong. The condition asks whether authority over the establishment and operation of the instrument is assigned to a specific governance actor. The question is not whether a jurisdiction holds environmental management authority. Portland plainly does. The question is what that authority is over. Three primary texts, none of them examined when version 3 was prepared, answer it. Portland City Code 17.39.010 states that the Bureau of Environmental Services "is authorized to facilitate the development and management of the City's storm sewer and drainage system facilities to adequately convey, manage and protect the water quality of discharges of stormwater runoff," and that the chapter applies to the City storm sewer and drainage systems as defined in it. The object of the codified authority is an infrastructure system. The verb is facilitate. Portland City Code chapter 33.430 contains the nearest analogue to an instrument in the zoning code, the natural resource management plan, which covers large ecosystems, carries management objectives, allowed and prohibited uses, timetables and approval criteria, and supersedes conflicting provisions of the chapter. Section 33.430.340 states that the applicant must submit such a plan, and section 33.430.330 makes its adoption a legislative procedure. No named governance actor holds authority over its establishment and operation; an applicant proposes and the Council adopts. The Portland Watershed Management Plan, on which the substantial score largely rested, was adopted by City Council Resolution No. 36384 of 8 March 2006. A resolution is not code. The watershed councils are formally recognised bodies constituted by charter, and the recognition carries no delegated decision authority. The arrangement that would carry this condition to substantial presence is therefore non-binding policy. Metro Code Title 13 assigns compliance obligations to cities and counties in respect of local comprehensive plans. That is authority over plan compliance, not over an instrument. Applying the boundary rule for this condition — authority assigned generally, without the instrument in scope, is partial — the cell is partial. How the error was found. A staged double reading under codebook rule 6.6, carried out for a subsequent case set covering the United States and Türkiye, produced a divergence on this cell: the first reading recorded substantial, the second partial. Rule 6.6 requires that a divergence be resolved at the step of the coding sequence at which the readings parted, which here was whether the instrument falls within the scope of the assigned authority. The primary texts were read for the resolution, and they settled it. This is a correction rather than a revision on new evidence. Portland City Code 17.39 and chapter 33.430 were in force throughout, and Resolution No. 36384 dates from 2006. The evidence was available when version 3 was prepared and was not read. Recording that distinction matters more than recording the new score: a reader is entitled to know whether a record changed because the world changed or because the record was wrong. description: Version 6 — references to unpublished text removed; factual corrections to sources; no score changed This version changes no score symbol and no numeric value. Earlier versions of this record referred in several places to an "associated manuscript" and, in one cell, to a "companion manuscript (FEIP)", and one column was named score_in_associated_manuscript. title: VarMeanHom-WS-US: Variability- and mean- homogenized daily near-surface wind speed dataset for the United States (1973–2024)
description: This dataset provides daily near-surface (10 m) wind speed for 592 stations in the contiguous United States over 1973–2024. The series are homogenized for both the mean and the variability (distributional width and upper tail) of daily wind speed. Station-specific changepoint information is also included. Input data. The input series (ws_in) is the mean-homogenized daily wind speed from the Global Homogenized Surface Wind Speed Dataset of Zhang and Wang (2024; https://doi.org/10.11888/Atmos.tpdc.301997 ), which is based on HadISD. That dataset adjusts only the mean. Each daily value within a year is scaled by a single annual factor, so inhomogeneities in variability can remain. Such inhomogeneities arise, for example, from the ASOS automation and the replacement of cup anemometers by ultrasonic sensors. Variability homogenization. Pre-processing. Stations were retained if they had at least 33 years that met the completeness criteria. Daily values ≤ 2 kt (≈ 1.03 m s⁻¹) were set to missing to exclude the effects of changes in calm-wind reporting and sensor starting thresholds. Variability index. The 1981–2010 daily climatology was removed from the daily series. An annual variability index was defined as the standard deviation of the resulting daily anomalies in each year. Reference series. A 20CRv3 10 m wind-speed variability series (1973–2015) was used as an independent reference, because surface wind observations are not assimilated into 20CRv3. Before use, the reference was itself checked for inhomogeneities and adjusted. The check used the number of assimilated pressure observations and the 10 m wind ensemble spread as auxiliary information. Changepoint detection. Changepoints in the station variability index were detected relative to the homogenized 20CRv3 reference with the PMT-based routines in RHtestsV4 (FindU.wRef, FindUD.wRef, StepSize.wRef). Candidates were cross-checked against ASOS commissioning records in the NOAA/NCEI HOMR and against the nationwide ASOS deployment (1992–2004) and sensor-replacement (2005–2008) periods. Daily adjustment. With the final changepoints fixed, the daily wind speeds themselves were adjusted by quantile matching (RHtestsV4 QMadj.GaussianDLY). 100 probability classes were used, and the most recent homogeneous segment served as the base segment. The adjustments were estimated from differences among the empirical distributions of the station’s own homogeneous segments. 20CRv3 data were not used in the adjustment. The adjustment was applied to the detrended series, so the long-term trend is preserved. Because the adjustment depends on cumulative probability, it can change the distributional width and upper tail, not only the mean. The adjusted daily series is ws_homo. In total, 1762 changepoints were identified at 581 stations, clustered in the mid-to-late 1990s and in 2005–2008. Contents. ws_in: input mean-homogenized daily wind speed (m s⁻¹). ws_homo: mean- and variability-homogenized daily wind speed (m s⁻¹). Station metadata (ID, latitude, longitude, elevation). Changepoint list for each station: dates, type (Type-1 statistical; Type-0 supported by station metadata or by the upgrade periods), and significance. Usage notes. Values ≤ 2 kt are missing in ws_homo. The dataset is therefore not suitable for analysing calm-wind frequency or the number of weak-wind days. Adjusted series are aligned to the most recent observing system (the final homogeneous segment). The 20CRv3 reference ends in 2015, so changepoint detection is less sensitive during 2016–2024. title: Water Plant Functional Group (WPFG) Database: Version 1
description: The Water Plant Functional Group (WPFG) Database collates existing assignments of wetland and aquatic plants to the Brock & Casanova (Brock & Casanova 1997; Casanova & Brock 2000; Casanova 2011) Water Plant Functional Group (WPFG) framework, which classifies plants according to their ecological responses to hydrological conditions. It harmonises taxonomy across historical source datasets assigning species to WPFG and synthesises the available classification evidence to provide species-level classifications under both the 7-category and 10-category WPFG systems. The two classification systems are treated as alternative levels of resolution rather than competing classifications. The database also provides a separate genus-level analysis describing the degree to which WPFG classifications are conserved among classified species within genera, together with historical WPFG assignments made explicitly at genus level. This information is provided as supporting evidence for users considering unclassified species; genus-level patterns are not used to infer or automatically assign species-level WPFG classifications. For both 7- and 10-category classifications, the user database reports the best-supported WPFG, second-ranked WPFG, their respective support, the margin between the top two alternative categories in terms of relative support, the number of contributing sources, dependence-adjusted effective evidence, and fuzzy membership across WPFG categories. Taxonomic names are harmonised using R package APCalign against an explicitly specified Australian Plant Census taxonomic resource. Original source names and classifications are retained to preserve provenance and enable auditing of the harmonisation and classification process. This Version 1 release contains five workbooks: WPFG_user_database_Ver1.xlsx — the principal user-facing database, including the WPFG decision database, taxonomic name lookup, genus summaries and underlying species-level evidence. plant_functional_group_master_Ver1.xlsx — the taxonomically harmonised master database and audit trail, including the original source records. WPFG_classification_analysis_Ver1.xlsx — detailed species-level classification analyses, assignment chains, fuzzy memberships and cross-classification outputs. WPFG_genus_analysis_Ver1.xlsx — descriptive analyses of WPFG conservation within genera and historical genus-level assignments. WPFG_validation_Ver1.xlsx — structural, weighting, hierarchical and sensitivity validation of the classification workflow. The database is generated by a reproducible R workflow maintained in the associated GitHub repository. Each database release is explicitly linked to a versioned source dataset, database version, Australian Plant Census resource/version, R workflow and package environment. Acknowledgements We acknowledge the substantial contributions of numerous researchers to the development of the Water Plant Functional Group classification and the data underlying this database. Margaret Brock was a co-author of the original classification with Michelle Casanova. Keith Ward, Daryl Nielsen and Patrick Driver contributed data to the Australia-wide WPFG database maintained by Michelle Casanova. Max Finlayson, Arnold van der Valk, Cassie James, Sam Capon, Adrian Clements, Ray Froend, Robert Godfree and Jane Roberts contributed to workshops and discussions that informed the development of the WPFG framework, held under the aegis of the Australian Centre for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis between 2012 and 2014. We gratefully acknowledge all of these researchers for their substantial contributions to the development of the database. title: Water balance and model validation data for experimental evapotranspiration tanks in the Brazilian Cerrado
description: This dataset contains interval-based observations and simulation outputs used to evaluate the water-balance model of three experimental evapotranspiration tanks (TEvap) in Cuiabá, Mato Grosso, Brazil. It supports the model-validation component of the manuscript “Hydrological performance and design thresholds of evapotranspiration tanks as a nature-based solution in the Brazilian Cerrado.” The dataset covers October 27, 2023, to August 9, 2024, and contains 87 records corresponding to 29 labeled intervals for each of three tanks (A, B, and C). There are 85 complete observed–simulated pairs for water storage change and mean daily tank evapotranspiration. Variables include interval dates and duration, tank area, observed and simulated storage at interval boundaries, precipitation and reference evapotranspiration totals, water storage changes, water-balance estimates of tank evapotranspiration, tank coefficients, and training and validation tank identifiers for the leave-one-tank-out cross-validation design. In this design, two tanks constitute the training group and the remaining tank constitutes the validation group. Water storage change is defined as final minus initial storage, with positive values indicating an increase and negative values indicating a decrease. Observed tank evapotranspiration is estimated from the interval water balance. Negative estimates are retained, and missing values are represented by blank fields; no missing values were imputed. Validation metrics include root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), bias (simulated minus observed), Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), and squared Pearson correlation (r²). Data are provided in CSV and Excel formats. Supporting files include a data dictionary with variable definitions and units, validation metrics, a copy of the source workbook, and a README describing file contents, calculation conventions, and scope. CSV files use UTF-8 encoding, comma delimiters, decimal points, and ISO-formatted dates. This deposit covers interval-based model validation. It does not include the complete experimental climate time series, stage–volume measurements, the 2003–2025 climate forcing, long-term design-scenario outputs, or the original model and calibration code. The supplied simulation outputs are preserved; simulations and calibration were not rerun during dataset preparation. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23344302

title: YASHASH BINOLARINI AVTONOM ENERGIYA BILAN TA'MINLASHNING ZAMONAVIY TEXNOLOGIYALARI VA ISTIQBOLLARI
description: Mazkur maqolada turar-joy binolarida avtonom elektr va issiqlik ta’minoti tizimlaridan foydalanish bo‘yicha xorijiy va mahalliy ilmiy tadqiqotlar tahlil qilingan. Quyosh fotoelektrik panellari, shamol turbinalari, biomassa qurilmalari, akkumulyatorlar va zaxira generatorlariga asoslangan gibrid energiya tizimlarining texnik, energetik, iqtisodiy hamda ekologik samaradorligi ko‘rib chiqilgan. Shuningdek, quyosh havo kollektorlari yordamida binolarni isitish, issiqlik energiyasini tejash va ichki haroratni barqaror saqlash imkoniyatlari yoritilgan. Tahlil natijalari avtonom energiya tizimlarining samaradorligi iqlim sharoitlari, energiya yuklamasi, qurilmalar konfiguratsiyasi va texnologiyalarning iqtisodiy ko‘rsatkichlariga bog‘liqligini ko‘rsatadi. Mavjud tadqiqotlarda elektr energiyasi ishlab chiqarishga katta e’tibor qaratilgan bo‘lsa-da, turar-joy binolarida avtonom elektrli issiq pol va havoli isitish tizimlarini o‘zaro uyg‘unlashtirish masalalari qo‘shimcha ilmiy izlanishlarni talab etadi.         DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23617257

title: ʻŌhiʻa Seed Collection Zones in the Hawaiian Islands
description: Rapid ʻŌhiʻa Death (ROD) caused by the pathogen called Ceratocystis is killing thousands of ʻōhiʻa ( Metrosideros ) trees (rapidohiadeath.org) and poses a serious risk to the health and future of native forests statewide. Research, new quarantine rules, and increased sanitation measures are underway to slow the spread of the disease and reduce the risk of spread. As part of the 2017-2019 ROD Strategic Response Plan, ʻōhiʻa seed collections occurred statewide. To mitigate the potential loss of genetic diversity and provide appropriate plant material for restoration, watershed rehabilitation, and saplings for research and testing for resistance or tolerance to the fungal disease, the ʻŌhiʻa Seed Collection Zone Maps were created to guide and track seed collections. The provisional maps are based on climate, topography, biogeography, and expert knowledge.  DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23245326

title: ГИБРИД ЭНЕРГИЯ ТИЗИМЛАРИ ЭЛЕМЕНТЛАРИНИ БОШҚАРИШ МУАММОЛАРИНИНГ ҲОЗИРГИ ҲОЛАТИ ТАҲЛИЛИ
description: Ушбу тезисда қайта тикланувчи энергия манбалари ва энергия сақлаш қурилмаларига асосланган гибрид энергетик тизимлар элементларини бошқариш муаммоларининг ҳозирги ҳолати таҳлил қилинган. Қуёш радиацияси ва шамол тезлигининг ўзгарувчанлиги туфайли генерация қувватининг беқарорлиги, электр энергиясини ишлаб чиқариш ва истеъмол қилиш ўртасидаги номутаносиблик ҳамда тизим ишончлилигини таъминлаш масалалари кўриб чиқилган. Максимал қувват нуқтасини кузатиш (MPPT), генетик алгоритм (GA), заррачалар тўдаси оптималлаштириш (PSO), сунъий нейрон тармоқлар (ANN) ва нейро-ноаниқ бошқарув (ANFIS) усулларининг имкониятлари ҳамда чекловлари таҳлил қилинган. Шунингдек, энергия таъминоти ишончлилиги, аккумуляторнинг заряд ҳолати (SOC) ва иқтисодий харажатларни ҳисобга олувчи кўп мезонли оптималлаштириш ёндашуви ёритилган. Таҳлил натижасида гибрид оптималлаштириш алгоритмлари ва сунъий интеллект технологияларини реал вақт режимида бошқарув тизимларига интеграциялаш истиқболли йўналиш сифатида белгиланган. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23494264

title: РАЗЛИЧИЯ ЭКОНОМИЧЕСКОГО РОСТА РАЗВИТЫХ И РАЗВИВАЮЩИХСЯ СТРАН
description: В статье рассматриваются основные различия экономического роста развитых и развивающихся стран. Особое внимание уделяется темпам роста валового внутреннего продукта, производительности труда, инвестициям, государственной поддержке, инфляции и качеству жизни населения. Исследование основано на сравнительном анализе материалов Международного валютного фонда, Всемирного банка и Организации экономического сотрудничества и развития. Анализ показывает, что развивающиеся экономики нередко демонстрируют более высокие темпы роста благодаря индустриализации, инвестициям и расширению внутреннего рынка. Вместе с тем результаты развития зависят от технологического уровня, качества институтов, структуры занятости и устойчивости макроэкономической политики. Сделан вывод о том, что устойчивый экономический рост предполагает не только увеличение объёма производства, но и повышение реальных доходов населения, развитие образования, здравоохранения и производительности труда. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23490172
